questions.explanation: Identifying needs. Developing specifications, or requirements, for the goods or services to be purchased is part of the first step of the purchasing process—identifying needs. Selecting suppliers involves searching for suppliers online, in trade publications, through advertisements, in catalogs, from salespeople, or at trade shows. Placing orders involves sending a purchase order to the supplier to indicate that the company is ready to make the purchase. Evaluating supplier performance is the last step of the purchasing process and involves reviewing the order and determining if the supplier followed through on its performance.
questions.piDescription: Explain the nature and scope of purchasing
questions.reference: LAP-OP-015—Buy Right (Purchasing)

questions.question: Thad wants to sell liquor from his restaurant, but he must first maintain government requirements and apply to be a liquor seller. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Licensing. Licensing is a method that government uses to regulate business by controlling who is allowed to function in the marketplace. In this case, Thad is trying to get a liquor license for his restaurant. Price controls refer to ceilings on how much a business can charge for a product. Zoning refers to regulations around property. Price discrimination occurs when businesses sell the same product at different prices depending on the customer.
questions.piDescription: Determine the relationship between government and business
questions.reference: LAP-EC-008—Regulate and Protect (Government and Business)

questions.question: Lumi, a fashion operations manager, must determine when fabric rolls arrive at the cutting tables and how long they remain before moving to the sewing stations. Lumi is responsible for
questions.explanation: Scheduling. Scheduling is an operations activity that establishes the timetable to be followed in production. It controls the flow of the entire production process by determining when materials will arrive at a certain destination and how long they will stay there. Routing involves selecting the sequence in which the steps of production need to be carried out. Logistics refers to managing the flow of goods and services from production to consumption. This includes all the people, information, and processes involved in storing and transporting goods. Expense control refers to keeping an eye on the bottom line. In this scenario, Lumi is not responsible for routing, logistics, or expense control.
questions.reference: LAP-OP-189—Smooth Operations (Nature of Operations)

questions.question: Suppose that new government regulations cause the price of fishing licenses to jump 120%. What effect is this likely to have on the market for fishing rods and equipment?

options.B: They will be taxed at lower rates.
options.C: They will be taxed at higher rates.

questions.explanation: Their demand will decrease. Fishing licenses and equipment like fishing rods are complementary goods. This means that changes in supply and demand of one good is likely to affect the other. In this case, the jump in fishing license prices is likely to decrease demand for fishing licenses and, as a result, decrease demand for fishing equipment. The demand for complementary goods does not have a direct effect on tax rates.
questions.piDescription: Explain the principles of supply and demand
questions.reference: LAP-EC-905—It's the Law (Supply and Demand)

questions.question: In a spreadsheet, which feature should a user employ to automatically change the formatting of a cell based on the specific value it contains?
questions.explanation: Conditional formatting. Conditional formatting is a specific tool designed to apply styles to cells only when they meet certain criteria, helping users visually highlight trends. Data validation is used to restrict the type of data or values that users can enter into a cell, rather than change its appearance. Goal seek is a “what-if” analysis tool used to find the input value needed to achieve a desired result in a formula. Pivot tables are used for exploring large datasets, not for styling individual cells based on their content.
questions.reference: University of York. (2026, January 27). Spreadsheet basics – Essential spreadsheets: a practical guide. Retrieved February 2, 2026, from https://subjectguides.york.ac.uk/spreadsheets/basics

questions.question: Vantage Point Analytics requires employees to change their passwords every 90 days and use two-factor authentication for all system logins. Which aspect of information management is this policy designed to address?
questions.explanation: Information security. Information security refers to the specific methods used to protect systems and data from unauthorized access or theft. Data transparency refers to the openness of an organization regarding how it collects and uses data. Information sharing focuses on how employees communicate information to one another. Data analysis is the process of inspecting data to discover useful information.
questions.piDescription: Explain information privacy, security, and confidentiality considerations in business
questions.reference: Holdsworth, J., & Kosinski, M. (n.d.). What is information security (InfoSec)? Retrieved February 2, 2026, from https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/information-security

questions.question: Raleigh, a marketing manager at Fourfold Furniture, is responsible for conducting market research to determine which new shelving units should be developed and whether the flat-pack boxes prevent scratches during shipping. Raleigh is performing which marketing function?
questions.explanation: Product/Service management. The product/service management marketing function involves obtaining, developing, maintaining, and improving a product or service mix in response to market opportunities. During this process, product/service management tries to answer questions such as “What new products should be developed?” and “Is the product packaged appropriately?” The pricing function involves determining and adjusting prices to maximize return and meet customers’ perceptions of value. Channel management is responsible for identifying, selecting, monitoring, and evaluating sales channels, also known as channels of distribution. The purpose of the promotion function is to communicate information about goods, services, images, or ideas to achieve a desired outcome.
questions.piDescription: Describe marketing functions and related activities
questions.reference: LAP-MK-002—Work the Big Seven (Marketing Functions)

questions.question: Each month, Unbundle Logistics pays for its insurance premiums, property taxes, and the flat-rate rent on its warehouse. These costs are __________ expenses.
questions.explanation: Fixed. Operating costs that do not increase or decrease with changes in production are called fixed costs or expenses. These are the expenses that must be paid no matter what. Examples of fixed expenses include insurance premiums, property taxes, rent/mortgage, wages/salaries, and insurance. Variable costs or expenses fluctuate with changes in production; examples include advertising and promotion, travel expenses, and sales commissions. Semi-variable costs are fixed until the company reaches a certain level of production; after that, they become variable. An example is a manufacturer that has a fixed cost for its employees’ wages, but pays more for overtime, which is a variable cost.
questions.piDescription: Explain the nature of overhead/operating costs
questions.reference: LAP-OP-024—Watch Your (Over) Head (Overhead/Operating Costs)

questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of a transferable skill gained through a school club that can substitute for formal work experience:

options.A: Managing a budget and scheduling meetings for the Art Club
options.B: Contributing to discussions and attending screenings for the Cinema Club
options.C: Maintaining a high follower count on social media
options.D: Participating in weekly practices for a local esports or gaming team

questions.explanation: Managing a budget and scheduling meetings for the Art Club. The responsibility involved with managing a budget and scheduling meetings is exactly what employers look for in entry level hires. This demonstrates functional experience that can be put on a resume even if the student hasn’t had a paycheck yet. Participating in weekly practices shows dedication, but gaming isn’t typically seen as a workplace substitute unless the student was organizing the event or managing a team. Unless the student is applying for a digital marketing role and can show how they grew the audience strategically, high followers are usually seen as personal rather than professional. Finally, contributing to discussions and attending film screenings are passive activities. They don’t demonstrate a specific skill (like leadership or organization) that a manager can use.
questions.piDescription: Describe techniques for obtaining work experience (e.g., volunteer activities, internships)
questions.reference: Herrity, J. (2025, December 16). Transferable skills: 10 skills that work across industries. Retrieved February 4, 2026, from https://www.indeed.com/career-advice/resumes-cover-letters/transferable-skills

questions.question: Bethany is reviewing sales figures to identify why a specific region underperformed last quarter. Which principle of data analysis is most important for ensuring the conclusions drawn are actually useful for decision-making?
questions.explanation: Integrity. Data integrity is a foundational principle; if the data are inaccurate, any subsequent analysis based on those data will be flawed. While having enough data is important, volume without relevance can obscure the actual insights needed to solve a problem. While visualization helps in communicating results, the aesthetic quality of a report is secondary to the reliability of the analysis. Data analysis usually aims to improve organizational performance. Isolating data often leads to silos that prevent collaborative problem-solving.
questions.piDescription: Explain the principles of data analysis
questions.reference: Salesforce. (2026). Guide to data integrity. Retrieved January 28, 2026, from https://www.salesforce.com/data/what-is-data-integrity/

questions.question: Implementing a new automated inventory system across a custom sneaker factory within nine months is an example of a __________ goal.
questions.explanation: Short term. A short-term goal typically takes under a year, while a long-term goal is achieved in more than a year. Performance-based goals focus on the outcome of the specific goal as opposed to the completion of it, and a learning goal deals with mastering a new skill.
questions.reference: LAP-PD-918—Go for the Goal (Goal Setting)

questions.question: Letty and Ishmael are having a conversation at a networking event. Ishmael tells Letty about some of his work projects. Letty holds eye contact, listens, and nods along as he speaks, but the conversation soon fizzles out. How could Letty have shown better active listening skills and kept the conversation going?
questions.explanation: Asking questions. Asking questions is an important part of active listening. It both demonstrates that the listener is paying attention and encourages more and deeper conversation. Letty was not distracted. She was focused on Ishmael while he spoke. Interrupting Ishmael would have been rude and might have given the impression that Letty was not interested in the conversation.
questions.reference: LAP-CO-017—Listen Up! (Demonstrating Active Listening Skills)

questions.question: Alfonso, a marketing manager, is deciding how best to use the company’s official LinkedIn account. Which of the following actions would be most appropriate:

options.A: Sending a private message to a friend
options.C: Changing the profile banner to his pet

questions.explanation: Reposting an industry news article. Business use is defined by strategic communication intended to build brand authority, engage a professional audience, and provide value to stakeholders or clients. Sharing his personal career journey does not align with professional organizational goals; Alfonso should focus on the official brand on the company account, not his story. Using a platform for private, non-work-related social interactions is the definition of personal use. Business profile elements should reflect corporate identity and branding; using personal photos is not representative of the company, but of an individual.
questions.piDescription: Distinguish between using social media for business and personal purposes
questions.reference: Kurtz, N. (2021, May 13). Shift your mindset: Social media for business vs. personal use. Retrieved January 27, 2026, from https://www.aducatedigital.com/advice/social-media-business-vs-personal-use/

questions.question: Jane notices one of her coworkers consistently falls asleep at their desk. She wonders if the employee is stressed since they are exhibiting
questions.explanation: Fatigue. When an employee is struggling to stay awake at their desk, they are exhibiting fatigue, which is a sign that they may be stressed out. Stress can cause trouble sleeping at night, which can lead to exhaustion during the day. Low morale refers to employees who are not excited about their work. Illness refers to physical health problems such as the cold or flu. Absenteeism occurs when employees either skip or miss work. This employee is not exhibiting low morale, illness, or absenteeism.
questions.piDescription: Explain the nature of stress management
questions.reference: LAP-EI-028—Keep Your Cool (Stress Management)

questions.question: During a business meeting, which of the following behaviors best demonstrates effective participation in a group discussion:
questions.explanation: Actively listening to others. Effective group participation involves active listening. Interrupting is unprofessional. Total silence prevents the group from benefiting from diverse perspectives and fails to fulfill the participants’ responsibility to contribute. Overusing technical jargon can alienate team members and hinder clear communication.
questions.reference: Indeed. (2025, December 16). 15 do’s and don’ts of group discussions. Retrieved January 28, 2026, from https://www.indeed.com/career-advice/career-development/dos-and-donts-of-group-discussion

questions.question: Assets with continually changing value, such as cash or inventory, are called __________ assets.
questions.explanation: Current. Assets with continually changing value, such as cash or inventory, are called current assets. Capital assets refer to property that a company permanently owns. Intangible assets are assets that are not physical in nature. Other assets are any assets not considered part of current or capital assets.
questions.piDescription: Explain the role of finance in business
questions.reference: LAP-FI-354—Money Matters (Role of Finance)

questions.question: Peak Chic sells high-quality clothes for low prices. Cotton Core has slightly higher prices but provides personal assistance, a clear return policy, and online shopping options. Which of the following is the most accurate statement:

options.A: Cotton Core is likely to be successful because it practices customer experience management.
options.B: Peak Chic is likely to be successful because it practices customer relationship management.
options.C: Cotton Core is unlikely to be successful because it has higher prices.
options.D: Peak Chic is unlikely to be successful because customers do not care about quality.

questions.explanation: Cotton Core is likely to be successful because it practices customer experience management. In an experience economy, customers often care as much about having positive experiences as they do about pricing, so a store with slightly higher prices is still likely to find success if it provides a great customer experience. Peak Chic does not practice customer relationship management. Customers do often care about quality.
questions.piDescription: Discuss the nature of customer relationship management
questions.reference: LAP-CR-016— Know When To Hold 'Em (Nature of Customer Relationship Management)

questions.question: Luca is shopping for a used motorhome. Which of the following should he do:

options.A: Determine his walk-away point before negotiating
options.C: Avoid negotiations to ensure a lower price
options.D: Go into negotiations without any preparation

questions.explanation: Determine his walk-away point before negotiating. Luca’s walk-away point is the highest price he would be willing to pay for a used motorhome. Knowing this beforehand would give him valuable preparation for negotiating his price and prevent him from overpaying. Going into negotiations blind is generally a bad idea. The salesperson’s first offer is not likely to be the best offer for Luca, so he should negotiate for an offer he is happy with. Avoiding negotiations does not guarantee a lower price.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-062—Make it a Win-Win (Negotiation in Business)

questions.question: Serena had audience members fill out surveys following her presentation. Some respondents said they were quickly hooked and enjoyed the included graphs, but were confused about the main point of the presentation. What characteristic of effective presentations does Serena need to improve on?

options.C: Having a great beginning and ending

questions.explanation: Presenting a clear message. Presentations should be clear in what they are trying to communicate. Serena’s audience indicated they were unsure about the main point of her presentation, implying her main points were unclear. Serena’s audience indicated that they were quickly engaged, so the beginning of her presentation was strong. They did not indicate confusion about her mannerisms or delivery. They also complimented her use of visual aids.
questions.reference: LAP-CO-025—Well Said! (Making Oral Presentations)

questions.question: Bellamy, a financial advisor, enters their client’s risk tolerance, income, and retirement expectations into a computer program designed to identify specific investment strategies. Bellamy is using a(n)
questions.explanation: Expert system. Expert systems are a special kind of computer software designed to mimic the knowledge of a human expert. For example, automotive mechanics, medical professionals, and financial advisors often use expert systems to diagnose issues and recommend solutions. This allows them to fix the problem more quickly. Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) is a type of technology that connects people quickly, either by voice or by voice and picture combined (think Zoom or FaceTime). Computer-aided design (CAD) is the use of technology and software to create, test, and rework products in the virtual world before spending money to produce them in the physical world. Global Positioning System (GPS) is a navigational system that uses satellite technology to determine location and provide directions.
questions.piDescription: Identify ways that technology impacts business
questions.reference: LAP-NF-003—TECH-tastic (Technology’s Impact on Business)

questions.question: Heart Tokyo is a fashionable clothing retailer that tries to appeal to a young, trendy audience. Its employees are required to wear stylish clothes, keep up with pop culture, and serve customers in a laid-back but professional manner. Which of the following touchpoints would be most consistent with Heart Tokyo’s brand promise:

options.C: Printed flyers and ads in the local newspaper
options.D: Short-form videos and promotions on social media

questions.explanation: Short-form videos and promotions on social media. Based on the requirements of its employees, young, trendy fashion and a laid-back atmosphere are part of Heart Tokyo’s brand promise. Modern advertising media, like short videos and social media, are therefore most consistent with its brand. Printed ads, word-of-mouth, email, and TV or radio ads are all less trendy touchpoints.
questions.reference: LAP-CR-001—Share the Promise (Identifying Brand Promise)

questions.question: Nala manages a small team of software developers. Two members approach her with a disagreement about how a feature should be implemented. Both ideas sound reasonable, but Nala would need to do some more research to determine which is better. What should she do?

options.A: Tell them both ideas make sense and they should just agree on one.
options.B: Tell them she will reflect on the issue and share her decision later.
options.C: Go with her gut and choose whichever implementation feels right.
options.D: Reject both ideas until she can come up with another idea they agree with.

questions.explanation: Tell them she will reflect on the issue and share her decision later. Pausing to reflect on new or conflicting ideas is key to considering them fully and openly. If Nala wants to come to the best decision, she should take the necessary time to determine the better option. Telling them to just agree on either idea does not solve the conflict or help the team. Making project decisions based on gut feelings is not generally a good idea. Rejecting ideas because they are not fully agreed upon will make it very hard to find good solutions.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-136—Pick a Side (Considering Conflicting Viewpoints)

questions.question: General Mills operates in the hypercompetitive market of breakfast cereals and needs to prioritize both product availability and order fulfillment. Which supply chain model is best suited for the company?
questions.explanation: Efficient. The efficient supply chain model is popular in markets where there is intense competition; companies aim to prioritize supply chain efficiency and delivery excellence over creating a product that stands out from the competition. This supply chain emphasizes the movement of the product, rather than the product itself. The efficient model prioritizes product availability and order fulfillment. General Mills focuses on end-to-end efficiency along its supply chain to reduce costs for both the company and its vendors. The flexible supply chain model is used by organizations in industries that typically experience periods of extremely high demand followed by periods of low demand. The fast supply chain model is best suited for trendy products in markets where demand changes rapidly. The continuous flow supply chain model emphasizes stability and consistency, and is typically employed in industries where supply and demand are predictable and secure.
questions.piDescription: Explain the concept of supply chain
questions.reference: LAP-OP-443—Deliver the Goods (Concept of Supply Chains)

questions.question: What is the first step an employee should take immediately after an accident occurs in the workplace, given they are not seriously injured?
questions.explanation: Notify a supervisor. Immediate reporting ensures that the company can initiate emergency protocols, secure the scene, and provide necessary medical attention or documentation. Filing an insurance claim is a secondary administrative step that occurs after the initial incident has been reported and documented. Cleaning the area before it is inspected can disturb evidence needed to determine the cause of the accident and prevent future occurrences. It is not necessary to scream for help if you are not seriously injured.
questions.reference: Centennial Medical Group. (n.d.). How to respond to workplace accidents and injuries. Retrieved February 2, 2026, from https://centennialmedical.com/how-to-respond-to-workplace-accidents- and-injuries/

questions.question: Investors analyze NimbusCore’s income statement and discover it has experienced consistent yearly profit growth. This positive trend in profitability suggests NimbusCore’s financial performance has been
questions.explanation: Successful. Before potential investors put their money into a business or buy any stock, they investigate whether the business expects to make a profit and how large the business expects that profit to be. A business with consistent yearly profit growth is appealing to investors; in other words, its financial performance has been successful. A business with fluctuating profits from year-to-year indicates its financial performance is average or inconsistent. There is no indication that Nimbus Core’s consistent yearly growth has been modeled.
questions.piDescription: Describe the nature of income statements
questions.reference: LAP-FI-094—Watch Your Bottom Line (Income Statements)

questions.question: Rekha is purchasing a milling machine for her company to start manufacturing custom parts. However, she is worried about buying a machine that does not work as advertised, resulting in a loss. How should Rekha mitigate this risk?

options.A: Avoid the risk by not buying a machine.
options.B: Prevent the risk by buying the cheapest option.
options.C: Buy a machine with a good warranty.
options.D: Control the risk by restricting use of the machine.

questions.explanation: Buy a machine with a good warranty. Rekha can avoid the risk of a faulty machine by transferring the risk to the company she is buying it from. This is done through a warranty which will guarantee a replacement if the machine does not work as intended. Rekha cannot avoid buying a machine. Restricting use of the machine does not prevent the machine from being faulty. Buying a cheaper machine does not decrease the chance that the machine will be faulty.
questions.reference: LAP-EC-911—Lose, Win, or Draw (Business Risk)

questions.question: Dominic has just finished a job interview for a retail position. What should he do next?

options.A: Visit the store the next day to ask other employees how he did.
options.B: Post a video on social media to discuss the questions he was asked.
options.C: Send a brief, personalized thank-you email within 24 hours.
options.D: Call the manager once a day until he receives a job offer.

questions.explanation: Send a brief, personalized thank-you email within 24 hours. Sending a thank-you message is a vital part of the post-interview procedure. It accomplishes three things: it shows professional courtesy, reinforces your interest in the position, and keeps your name top of mind for the hiring manager while they are making their final decision. Calling the manager each day would be bothersome, visiting the store to question other employees would be inappropriate, and posting a video on social media would be ineffective in securing a job offer.
questions.reference: Indeed. (2025, December 19). What to do after an interview: 9 tips to help you succeed. Retrieved February 4, 2026, from https://www.indeed.com/career-advice/interviewing/what-to-do-after-an-interview

questions.question: Isaac realizes he made a mistake that may delay a project past its deadline. Which of the following is the most likely consequence of Isaac hiding this mistake from his manager:

options.A: Isaac’s mistake will not be discovered and the project will hit its deadline.
options.B: Isaac’s mistake will be discovered and the project will miss its deadline.
options.C: Isaac’s manager will notice the project is behind schedule and will ignore it.
options.D: Isaac’s manager will notice the project is behind schedule and will fix it.

questions.explanation: Isaac’s mistake will be discovered and the project will miss its deadline. Transparent and honest communication can be difficult, but one of its benefits is that it can help resolve mistakes and conflicts. If Isaac hides his mistake and lets the project fall behind, it is likely that his mistake, as well as the fact that he hid it from his manager, will come to light. Isaac’s manager will likely notice the project is behind schedule and will not ignore it, but Isaac cannot rely on his manager simply fixing everything without any other consequences.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-129—Can We Talk? (Fostering Open, Honest Communication)

questions.question: After conducting an environmental scan, Caterpillar Consulting noticed a shift in consumer behavior: customers are increasingly concerned about sustainability and want to support businesses that align with their values. This trend falls under what category of information?
questions.explanation: Society and culture. Society is transforming at a rapid rate—some say faster than ever before. Successful businesses stay on top of changes in society and culture so that they can remain sensitive to customer needs and wants. Customers becoming increasingly concerned about sustainability and wanting to support values-aligned businesses is an example of a social trend in environmental scanning. Demographics are the physical and social characteristics of the population. An environmental scan may gather information on competition in a few different categories, such as brand competition, substitute products, or general competition. Economic factors that businesses should pay attention to during an environmental scan include inflation, unemployment rates, and interest rates. This scenario does not fall under demographics, competition, or the economy.
questions.piDescription: Conduct an environmental scan to obtain business information
questions.reference: LAP-NF-015—Get the 4-1-1 (Conducting an Environmental Scan)

questions.question: Which of the following is a routine security precaution a business should implement to protect physical assets:

options.B: Storing backup hard drives in an open drawer
options.D: Sharing office keys with all staff

questions.explanation: Implementing a clear desk policy. A clear desk policy ensures that sensitive information is secured in locked storage, reducing the risk of unauthorized access or theft. Limiting the distribution of physical keys is a standard security measure. Widespread access increases the risk of lost keys or internal theft. Leaving computer monitors on can expose data to unauthorized users. Backup media contains critical business data and must be stored in a secure location.
questions.reference: American Alarm. (2025, March 13). Five best practices to secure your business during off-hours. Retrieved February 2, 2026, from https://www.americanalarm.com/blog/five-best-practices-to-secure-your-business-during-off-hours-027515

questions.question: A customer asks you how long it will take for their order to come in. Which of the following responses best demonstrates a customer service mindset:

options.A: “It should arrive by the 21st. I will email you with any updates.”
options.B: “I’m not sure. Wait a moment while I check with my manager.”
options.C: “Call back later and somebody should be able to answer that for you.”
options.D: “If I had to guess, I’d say about two weeks or so.”

questions.explanation: “It should arrive by the 21st. I will email you with any updates.” Courteous, efficient responses to customers’ questions indicate that you have a customer service mindset. This response best indicates you have a customer service mindset because not only is it both courteous and efficient, but it also communicates that you are knowledgeable and willing to support them until their needs are met. The other responses are not very efficient or courteous, and they communicate a lack of knowledge.
questions.reference: LAP-CR-004—Set Your Mind to It (Customer Service Mindset)

questions.question: Three of the most significant benefits of inspiring others include personal satisfaction, more engaged peers and coworkers, and
questions.explanation: A reputation for leadership. Serving as an inspiration for others can help solidify your reputation as a leader. When you inspire others, people will begin to recognize you as someone to look to for guidance and support – in other words, as a leader. Inspiring others does not guarantee career success or an immediate salary raise, but it can help you obtain new opportunities. Inspiring others does not result in fewer responsibilities at work.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-133—A Force for Good (Inspiring Others)

questions.question: Bella works at the concierge desk at a hotel. One day, a guest approaches Bella asking for extra towels, but they want to be certain that they will not be charged extra. Despite Bella assuring the customer that they won’t, the guest asks to speak with her supervisor to confirm. What type of difficult customer is Bella dealing with?
questions.explanation: Suspicious. A suspicious customer doubts or questions everything and may want facts and proof before being convinced something is true. An argumentative customer seems to disagree, question, or look for errors in almost everything and everybody. An insulting customer intentionally makes unpleasant remarks or uses foul language. A slow/methodical customer requires a lot of time to make a purchase because of indecisiveness.
questions.reference: LAP-CR-009—Making Mad Glad (Handling Difficult Customers)

questions.question: To maintain high security standards for a business’s online banking accounts, which of the following practices should an administrative assistant follow:

options.A: Store account credentials in a shared document.
options.B: Implement a schedule for regular password updates.
options.C: Use the same password across all platforms for simplicity.

questions.explanation: Implement a schedule for regular password updates. Updating passwords regularly minimizes the risk of unauthorized access. Password recycling is a major security flaw. If one account is compromised, every other account using that password becomes vulnerable. Multi-factor authentication provides a critical second layer of security that prevents hackers from accessing accounts with only a stolen password. Disabling it would be unwise. Storing account credentials in a shared document makes login credentials easily accessible to whoever has access to the document.
questions.reference: General Electric Credit Union. (2026). Essential tips for managing your business checking account. Retrieved January 28, 2026, from https://www.gecreditunion.org/learn/education/resources/money-minutes/january-2024/essential-tips-for-managing-your-business-checking-account

questions.question: Faith just started a new role as a quality control specialist. Faith is working in __________ management.
questions.explanation: Operations. Operations management focuses on planning, organizing, coordinating, and controlling the resources needed to produce or provide a business’s goods or services. Quality control falls under this category. Human resources management focuses on the staffing activities that involve planning, recruitment, selection, orientation, and training. General management are employees who have supervisory responsibilities and make decisions. Finally, business information management is an umbrella term that covers careers that provide a bridge between business processes or initiatives and IT.
questions.reference: LAP-PD-025—Go for It! (Careers in Business)

questions.question: Ellison, a project manager at a tech start-up, determines the most likely amount of time it will take to develop a new delivery drone, as well as the best-case and worst-case scenarios. He then calculates the average. Ellison used __________ to assess the project’s human resource needs.
questions.explanation: Three-point estimating. Three-point estimating is a technique that considers the ways uncertainty and risk can affect estimates. It finds the average between the most likely, the worst-case, and the best-case scenarios. Bottom-up estimating is a method of estimating resources by adding up estimates for smaller components of the project. Short-range forecasting is a sales forecasting technique that predicts sales for periods of less than three months; it is used to aid in day-to-day decision-making regarding planning, scheduling, staffing, inventory, etc. There is no indication that Ellison used previous experience to assess the project’s human resource needs.
questions.reference: LAP-OP-003—Get What You Need (Identifying Project Resources)

questions.question: Insurance is best described as a(n)
questions.explanation: Risk management tool. Insurance is based on the principle of risk transfer: the policyholder pays a premium to an insurance company, which then agrees to compensate the policyholder for specific financial losses. The primary purpose of insurance is risk protection. It is not a savings plan. An investment strategy is a customized plan that guides an investor’s financial decisions. A government mandate is a regulatory requirement unrelated to transferring risk through insurance policies.
questions.reference: Kagan, J. (2025, December 29). What is insurance? Retrieved January 28, 2026, from https://www.investopedia.com/terms/i/insurance.asp

questions.question: Liv’s Linoleum is a small company that sells a small line of renter-friendly DIY wall and flooring solutions. It has been in business for many years and has a stable customer base. Most employees specialize in just one or two business activities. Liv’s Linoleum should use a __________ organizational design.
questions.explanation: Functional. A functional organizational design consists of traditional departments with specialized responsibilities like sales, marketing, and legal matters. It is ideal for small companies with stable demand for a small line of products. It also works well with specialized employees, making it a great choice for Liv’s Linoleum. A divisional structure is more dynamic, and useful for complex or fast-paced business environments. A matrix structure is a combination of divisional and functional structures and is more suitable for companies with large, complex projects. Lateral relations refers to the amount of teamwork found in an organizational design, not a design itself.
questions.piDescription: Explain the organizational design of businesses
questions.reference: LAP-EC-103—Designed to Work (Organizational Design of Businesses)

questions.question: A marketing team notices a positive correlation between social media engagement and weekly sales figures. Which of the following is the most accurate interpretation of this finding:

options.A: Social media ads are the most effective marketing tool.
options.B: Low social media engagement is the direct cause of poor sales.
options.C: Increasing social media engagement is guaranteed to increase sales.
options.D: Sales tend to rise as social media engagement increases.

questions.explanation: Sales tend to rise as social media engagement increases. A positive correlation indicates that two variables move in the same direction, but it does not inherently prove that one causes the other. Correlation does not imply absolute certainty or a guarantee of future performance. The statement that low social media engagement is the direct cause of poor sales assumes a causal relationship that might not exist. The marketing team’s findings only describe a relationship between engagement and sales. It does not compare the effectiveness of social media to other marketing tools.
questions.reference: Korem, A. (2025, August 7). A comprehensive guide to statistical significance. Retrieved February 2, 2026, from https://www.statsig.com/perspectives/a-comprehensive-guide-to-statistical-significance

questions.question: The CEO of a major computer chip manufacturer lies about the performance of its products. When the lie was exposed, the CEO immediately resigned. However, the company suffered a permanent loss of market share. Which of the following is the primary reason why the company failed to recover its market share after the CEO’s resignation:

options.A: The damage to the brand’s integrity permanently eroded public trust.
options.B: The company’s legal defense costs depleted its research and development budget.
options.C: The company faced mandatory criminal prosecution that prevented future sales.
options.D: The costs of the executive severance package created a permanent financial burden.

questions.explanation: The damage to the brand’s integrity permanently eroded public trust. The damage that a scandal causes to a company’s reputation and integrity can long outlive the scandal itself. One major scandal is sometimes enough to cause permanent damage to a company’s prospects. There is no indication that the company faced criminal prosecution or that the costs of a severance package were burdensome. A company would not likely use its research and development budget to pay for legal costs.
questions.piDescription: Explain the nature of business ethics
questions.reference: LAP-EC-106—On the Up and Up (Business Ethics)

questions.question: Which of the following elements is required for a contract to be considered legally binding:

options.A: There must be an offer, an acceptance, and an exchange of value.
options.B: The contract must be printed on official government-issued paper.
options.C: All parties involved must be at least 21 years of age.
options.D: The agreement must be signed in the presence of a judge.

questions.explanation: There must be an offer, an acceptance, and an exchange of value. The fundamental pillars of a contract include a clear offer, an acceptance, and consideration, meaning each party must provide something of value to the other. Most business contracts do not require a judge to be present to be valid. The legal age to enter most contracts is 18, not 21, in most jurisdictions. There is no legal requirement regarding the specific type of paper used for a contract. Contracts can be written on plain paper or, in some cases, agreed upon orally.
questions.piDescription: Describe the nature of legally binding contracts
questions.reference: Stim, R. (2024, July 25). What is a contract? Retrieved January 27, 2026, from https://www.nolo.com/legal-encyclopedia/contracts-basics-33367.html

questions.question: Monty is about to send a formal email to a potential client, but notices several grammatical errors and realizes that the tone may be too casual. What should he do?

options.A: Correct punctuation and ensure the tone is appropriate.
options.B: Delete the draft and try again the next day.
options.C: Ask his coworker to write their own draft and compare.
options.D: Ignore the errors and send the email immediately.

questions.explanation: Correct punctuation and ensure the tone is right. Professional editing and revising standards involve checking for both technical accuracy and stylistic appropriateness. Ignoring the errors and sending the email immediately is not only unprofessional but can create misunderstandings. Asking somebody else to write a draft and then comparing is unnecessary and inefficient. Deleting the draft and trying again the next day creates more work and delays the recipient from receiving the message.
questions.piDescription: Edit and revise written work consistent with professional standards
questions.reference: American Journal Experts. (2024, June 4). The writing process: Revising, editing, and proofreading. Retrieved January 27, 2026, from https://www.aje.com/arc/the-writing-process-revising-editing-and-proofreading
reviewNotes: info: rationale does not start with the correct option's text (source wording differs)

questions.question: Maki is a customer service representative for a pneumatics manufacturer and she wants to position herself to be promoted. How could Maki start showing initiative?

options.A: Start learning more about her company’s products.
options.B: Start skipping calls to talk to her coworkers.
options.C: Start improvising customer calls instead of using her script.
options.D: Start attending meetings she was not invited to.

questions.explanation: Start learning more about her company’s products. One way Maki could show initiative is by learning more about her company’s products, as this would demonstrate her interest in going beyond her job requirements. Improvising customer calls, attending meetings without an invitation, and skipping calls with clients may be seen as disrespectful, lazy, or insubordinate.
questions.piDescription: Explain the importance of demonstrating initiative
questions.reference: LAP-EI-024—Hustle! (Taking Initiative)

questions.question: Lucille’s project is already over budget, despite being far from finished. This is a sign that the
questions.explanation: Budget should be reevaluated. Project budgets should regularly be reevaluated to be as accurate as possible. A project going over budget is a sign that the budget should be reassessed. Projects often go over budget, so cancelling a project for this reason would be extreme. Similarly, going over budget does not mean a project will fail. The budget cannot remain the same because the project has already used up all its money.
questions.reference: LAP-FI-106—Money Tracks (Nature of Budgets)

questions.question: Lowered morale, higher turnover in the workplace, and decreased productivity are likely all results of

options.B: the hiring of a new company CEO.

questions.explanation: A leader abusing their power. A leader that abuses their power brings down morale by causing followers to feel anxious and intimidated. This can lead to higher turnover in workplaces, since employees are unlikely to remain at a company where they feel threatened or disrespected. Productivity is also harmed when leaders abuse their power—because followers lose their motivation and inspiration to do good work. Lowered morale, high turnover, and decreased productivity are not necessarily results of the hiring of a new CEO, giving employees paid vacation, or hosting social events at work.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-135—Power Play (Use Power Appropriately)

questions.question: Staff communication is best described as a(n) __________ process.
questions.explanation: Multi-directional. Staff communication is inherently multi-directional, serving functional purposes like coordination as well as social purposes like team building. Staff communication is not a one-way process. While informal communication exists, staff communication primarily encompasses the professional exchange of information necessary for business operations. Communication is a continuous, daily requirement for business success, not an annual event.
questions.piDescription: Explain the nature of staff communication
questions.reference: Indeed. (2025, November 27). What are staff communications (Types and importance). Retrieved January 27, 2026, from https://uk.indeed.com/career-advice/career-development/staff-communications

questions.question: Management at NearDesk believes that remote work has significantly decreased company productivity. When survey responses reveal that productivity has remained stable or even increased, they simply disregard the contradictory information during their quarterly review. This is a challenge related to __________ information.
questions.explanation: Evaluating. Interpreting or evaluating information without bias is a central tenet of ethical information management. One type of bias businesses must watch out for is confirmation bias. Confirmation bias is the tendency to agree with information or ideas that support one’s preexisting beliefs. A company like NearDesk might ignore data that contradict its perspectives or prop up questionable data that support them. Maintaining information refers to storing information in a safe and responsible manner. Accessing information refers to collecting information without violating user privacy. Disseminating information refers to sharing data fairly and sensibly. NearDesk is not experiencing a challenge related to maintaining, accessing, or disseminating information.
questions.piDescription: Explain the role of ethics in information management
questions.reference: LAP-NF-111—FYI (Ethics in Information Management)

questions.question: Luna is part of the bargaining team in her industry union. She knows the main concession that union members want is a wage increase. What kind of research might she perform in preparation for this issue?

options.D: Compile surveys from highly paid employees

questions.explanation: Analyze company financial reports. In preparation for a bargaining session, union representatives are likely to gather research that will inform and support their position. To determine if a company can afford to increase wages, Luna may wish to analyze its finances. Safety complaints may be part of a bargaining session but do not directly relate to wages. Similarly, records of disciplinary action will not help Luna bargain for higher wages. Highly paid employees are less likely to care about getting higher wages, and data from these surveys would not represent the average worker.
questions.piDescription: Explain the concept of organized labor and business
questions.reference: LAP-EC-915—Get United (Organized Labor)

questions.question: A wet floor in a busy hallway is best described as a(n) __________, while the likelihood that a customer or employee will slip and get injured is a(n) __________.
questions.explanation: Hazard; risk. A wet floor in a busy hallway is best described as a hazard, while the likelihood that a customer or employee will slip and get injured is a risk. A hazard is a potential source of harm or danger (e.g., chemicals, viruses, spills, power tools), while a risk is the chance or likelihood that someone could be hurt or injured from the hazard. An accident is an unplanned event that leads to harm. While an accident can occur due to a slip, the wet floor itself is not an accident. Personal protective equipment is used to prevent injury and includes helmets, safety goggles, masks, etc.
questions.piDescription: Describe health and safety regulations in business
questions.reference: HASpod. (2025, June 25). The difference between hazard and risk explained. Retrieved March 11, 2026, from https://www.haspod.com/blog/management/difference-between-hazard-risk-explained

questions.question: Anita, a small business owner, is evaluating her risk management strategy. Which of the following factors is most important to consider when determining the specific insurance needs of her business:

options.A: The current marketing budget and the projected growth of the economy
options.B: The nature of her business operations and the impact of specific risks
options.C: The personal credit scores of employees and Anita’s personal investment portfolio
options.D: The total number of years in the industry and the number of local competitors

questions.explanation: The nature of her business operations and the impact of specific risks. Identifying insurance needs requires an analysis of the specific risks associated with the business type and the financial severity of those potential losses. While experience is valuable for management, it does not dictate the types of coverage required to protect assets or mitigate legal liabilities. A marketing budget reflects growth strategy and spending, not the underlying risks that require financial protection through insurance policies. Employee credit scores are generally irrelevant to determining the business’s need for coverage.
questions.reference: Kagan, J. (2025, December 29). What is insurance? Retrieved January 28, 2026, from https://www.investopedia.com/terms/i/insurance.asp

questions.question: Alice is searching for reliable financial data to support a new business proposal. Which of the following sources would provide the most relevant and valid material:

options.A: A trending post on a popular social media platform
options.B: An undated wiki page that allows public edits
options.C: A personal blog written by a former employee of a competitor
options.D: A peer-reviewed journal article from a professional database

questions.explanation: A peer-reviewed journal article from a professional database. Peer-reviewed journals undergo rigorous evaluation by industry experts, ensuring the information is fact-checked, credible, and academically sound. Social media posts often prioritize engagement over accuracy and may contain personal bias or unverified claims. Personal blogs are subjective and may be influenced by the author’s personal experiences or grievances rather than objective data. Wiki pages that allow public edits lack accountability and can be changed by anyone, making the validity and timeliness of the information unreliable for business decisions.
questions.piDescription: Identify sources that provide relevant, valid written material
questions.reference: Purdue University. (2025). Evaluating sources: General guidelines. Retrieved January 28, 2026, from https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_inf ormation/general_guidelines.html

questions.question: GreenLeaf Urban Markets needs to store large amounts of customer data that can easily be referenced by multiple departments. Which of the following is the most effective tool for this purpose:
questions.explanation: Database management system. A database management system is specifically designed to store data in a way that allows for use by multiple departments. Word processors are designed for document creation, making them inefficient for referencing large sets of data. Cloud drives store files like PDFs or images. They do not inherently provide the data organization found in a database. Presentation software is intended for displaying information to an audience, not for long-term data storage.
questions.reference: Salesforce. (2026). 7 best practices for successful data management. Retrieved February 2, 2026, from https://www.tableau.com/learn/articles/data-management-best-practices

questions.question: Which of the following data mining techniques is primarily used to discover rules that describe specific data patterns, such as “customers who buy coffee also tend to buy sugar”:
questions.explanation: Association rule mining. Association rule mining identifies relationships or co-occurrences between variables in large datasets; it is frequently used in market basket analysis to see which products are bought together. Classification mining assigns items into predefined categories or classes based on historical data. Clustering mining groups data points together based on similarities without using predefined labels or rules. Regression mining is a statistical technique used to predict a continuous numerical value based on the relationship between variables.
questions.reference: Uniyal, M. (2025, January 27). Association rule mining. Retrieved February 2, 2026, from https://www.appliedaicourse.com/blog/association-rule-mining/

questions.question: Dean needs to present the sequential phases of a product launch to his team to ensure everyone understands the timeline. The organizational method most effective for this purpose is __________ organization.
questions.explanation: Chronological. Chronological organization arranges information in the order of events. For a project launch, this allows team members to see the progression of tasks over time. Alphabetical order is useful for indexing, but it would scramble the logic of a timeline based on the names of tasks. Geographical organization is based on physical location and does not help communicate a sequence of events. The deductive method is used to present a main conclusion followed by supporting details, which is effective for reports but less effective for illustrating a step-by-step schedule.
questions.reference: Indeed. (2025, December 11). How to create an effective product launch timeline (with steps). Retrieved January 27, 2026, from https://www.indeed.com/career-advice/career-development/product-launch-timeline

questions.question: Reagan makes a large purchase on her credit card with a 10% APR and decides to pay minimums on it rather than paying it off all at once. The total amount Reagan pays will be

options.A: more than if she paid her statement in full.
options.B: the exact amount she made the purchase for.
options.C: $0 or close to $0 after interest fees and returns.
options.D: less than if she paid her statement in full.

questions.explanation: More than if she paid her statement in full. Paying a credit card statement down via minimums generally increases the total amount owed by a percentage rate such as APR. Reagan will therefore end up paying more than she would have if she paid the statement in full.
questions.piDescription: Explain the purposes and importance of credit
questions.reference: LAP-FI-002—Give Credit Where Credit Is Due (Credit and Its Importance)

questions.question: One of the main responsibilities of the Human Resources (HR) department is to ensure that the right people are working in the right positions. Which of the following HR activities is most directly related to this responsibility:
questions.explanation: Recruiting and selecting new employees. HR managers recruit, interview, and select employees to make sure the organization has qualified people in appropriate roles. Managing the company’s finances is a financial activity. Advertising the company’s products is a marketing activity. While administering compensation and benefits is a key HR function for attracting and retaining talent, it is not the direct activity responsible for initially matching a person’s skills and potential to a specific job opening. That function is handled by recruiting and selection (staffing).
questions.piDescription: Discuss the nature of human resources management
questions.reference: LAP-HR-410—People Pusher (Nature of Human Resources Management)

questions.question: A potential investor is trying to decide if a local bowling alley would be a sound investment. Which of the following represents the most relevant financial information for this decision:

options.A: The cost of the building that houses the bowling alley
options.B: The bowling alley’s profit over the past five years
options.C: The average number of visits per member, per year
options.D: The average wage of the bowling alley’s employees

questions.explanation: The bowling alley’s profit over the past five years. Investors mainly look for a return on their investment, so a business’s profits over five years gives the most relevant picture of its financial potential. The wages of its employees are a single cost of business that don’t give a clear picture of the alley’s finances as a whole. Similarly, visits per member is a single metric of limited importance to investing. The cost of the company building represents an asset that does not tell an investor much about the success of the business.
questions.piDescription: Describe the need for financial information
questions.reference: LAP-FI-579—By the Numbers (The Need for Financial Information)

questions.question: Maya, a marketing assistant, has a creative idea for a new campaign, but her direct supervisor is on vacation. Instead of waiting or speaking to the assistant manager, Maya emails the CEO to pitch her idea. Why is this action considered a violation of the chain of command?

options.A: Because internal ideas must always be delivered via face-to-face discussion, not email
options.B: Because a marketing assistant’s primary role is administrative support, not creative strategy
options.C: Because she bypassed the intermediate levels of authority responsible for her department
options.D: Because the CEO is the only individual authorized to make final marketing decisions

questions.explanation: Because she bypassed the intermediate levels of authority responsible for her department. In business administration, the chain of command ensures that communication and authority flow through specific levels. By going straight to the CEO, Maya ignores the managers who are responsible for their daily work. This can lead to the CEO being overwhelmed with small tasks and the direct managers feeling undermined or out of the loop regarding their own team’s projects. Employees at all levels are encouraged to be creative; the issue is how they communicate them. While a CEO has final say on strategies, they hire managers so they don’t have to make every small departmental decision. Internal ideas can be delivered in a variety of formats. The email wasn’t the problem—the recipient (the CEO) was.
questions.reference: LAP-PD-252—Don’t Cheat the Chain (Following Chain of Command)

questions.question: Which of the following is the most effective example of a SMART financial goal for a startup company:

options.A: To invest a significant portion of monthly profits into the stock market to build a rainy-day fund
options.B: To become the most profitable company in the local region as quickly as possible
options.C: To increase total revenue by 15% through the expansion of online sales by December 31
options.D: To reduce business expenses by cutting unnecessary costs across all departments

questions.explanation: To increase total revenue by 15% through the expansion of online sales by December 31. This goal is SMART because it identifies a clear target, a method, and a deadline. Becoming the most profitable company in the local region as quickly as possible is too vague a goal and lacks a specific metric for success or a defined timeframe. Reducing business expenses by cutting unnecessary costs across all departments, while a good business practice, states a general intention rather than a goal—it does not specify how much costs should be cut or by when. Investing a significant portion of monthly profits into the stock market to build a rainy-day fund describes a financial strategy but lacks the measurable targets and time constraints required for a formal financial goal.
questions.reference: Martins, J. (2026, January 5). What are SMART goals? Examples and templates. Retrieved January 28, 2026, from https://asana.com/resources/smart-goals

questions.question: Gibson is an intern at a wildlife research center. His manager tells him during a performance review that he should be more receptive to feedback from his peers. How can Gibson be more receptive?

options.A: Keep his workspace neat and prioritize tasks
options.B: Compromise and work together with his peers
options.C: Have a positive attitude and listen to criticism
options.D: Speak with more confidence and authority

questions.explanation: Have a positive attitude and listen to criticism. Receptivity is the trait of open-mindedness, especially to criticism and feedback. Having a positive attitude and listening to criticism is a clear way to demonstrate receptivity. Keeping a workspace clean and prioritizing tasks is part of having organizational skills. Compromising and working with peers demonstrates cooperativeness. Speaking with confidence and authority demonstrates assertiveness.
questions.piDescription: Identify desirable personality traits important to business
questions.reference: LAP-EI-918—You’ve Got Personality (Personality Traits in Business)

questions.question: After analyzing its production processes, Hammer & Forge realizes its assembly line workers must walk five extra steps to reach their tool stations. Which of the seven wastes of lean production did the company identify?
questions.explanation: Motion. Lean production originated with the car manufacturer Toyota. The foundation of lean is maximizing customer value while minimizing waste. Waste is anything that doesn’t create value for the customer. Motion refers to the wear and tear that production puts on both workers and equipment. Employees and machinery should be preserved from unnecessary work as much as possible. Over-processing refers to putting any more work or materials into a product than the customer needs; it wastes time and money and does not create any added value. Waiting refers to having products sitting around waiting to be worked on or sold, which wastes time and does not add value. Defective products cause companies to waste time fixing them or to lose money not being able to sell them.
questions.reference: LAP-OP-163—Take Control (Quality-Control Measures)

questions.question: Ron manages a team of engineers. After nearly missing a major deadline, he decides to start assigning tasks to pairs of engineers instead of individuals. He finds that tasks get completed faster and more consistently. This is an example of collaboration

options.C: at the cost of speed and efficiency.

questions.explanation: Increasing employee performance. Collaboration between employees can increase performance because each individual has strengths and weaknesses that contribute to project quality and speed. Collaboration can also make work more motivating and engaging for employees. In Ron’s case, fostering collaboration among his team increased the rate at which they completed their tasks. Ron’s team did not increase innovation or lose speed and efficiency. Assigning tasks to pairs of engineers was a strategy, not a punishment.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-130—Genius Is a Team Sport (Collaborating With Others)

questions.question: Jocelyn was recently let go from her customer service position due to downsizing. Which of the following could be considered a ‘silver lining’ to her unemployment:

options.A: She can reexamine her talents, skills, and desires.
options.B: She is entering a very competitive job market.
options.C: She will have difficulty paying her bills.

questions.explanation: She can reexamine her talents, skills, and desires. A silver lining to unemployment is that it forces laid-off workers to reexamine their talents, skills, and desires, which may lead to more personal happiness as well as a better allocation of resources within the economy. Having difficulty paying bills, entering a very competitive job market, and experiencing self-doubt are all negative consequences of unemployment.
questions.piDescription: Discuss the impact of a nation's unemployment rates
questions.reference: LAP-EC-082—Help Wanted (Impact of Unemployment Rates)

questions.question: VelaSource, a software company, has developed a unique piece of source code that gives it a competitive advantage. It chooses to keep the code private rather than filing for public legal protection. Which method of intellectual property protection is VelaSource using?
questions.explanation: Trade secret. A trade secret consists of confidential business information that provides an edge over competitors and is protected through internal security measures rather than government registration. A patent requires the inventor to publicly disclose the details of the invention in exchange for exclusive rights for a limited time. Trademarks protect brand identifiers like logos, names, and slogans, but not source code. While copyright protects the expression of code, it does not protect the underlying secrets if the company’s primary strategy is to keep the information hidden from the public.
questions.piDescription: Describe methods used to protect intellectual property
questions.reference: Moore, S. (2024, June 27). How to protect your intellectual property. Retrieved January 27, 2026, from https://www.forbes.com/sites/schuylermoore/2024/06/27/how-to-protect-your-intellectual-property/

questions.question: Maria, a client relations manager, tells her team, “Our goal for this quarter is to provide much better customer service than we did last quarter.” Why does this goal fail to function as an effective organizational tool?

options.A: It is not measurable, making it impossible to track progress.
options.B: It is a personal goal rather than a business goal.
options.C: It is too challenging for entry-level employees to achieve.
options.D: It focuses on the customer rather than on making a profit.

questions.explanation: It is not measurable, making it impossible to track progress. For a goal to function properly, it must be measurable. Phrases like “much better” or “improved” are subjective—everyone has a different opinion on what better looks like. An effective version of this goal would include a metric, such as increasing customer satisfaction survey scores from 80% to 90% by the end of the quarter. It’s impossible to judge if it’s too challenging or easy because the goal is too vague to define the work required. Customer service goals are essential business goals. High-quality service usually leads to higher long-term profits. This is a business goal because it involves the team and customer service, which are organizational elements.
questions.piDescription: Determine the nature of organizational goals
questions.reference: Indeed. (2025, November 19). What are organizational goals? (And why they are important). Retrieved February 4, 2026, from https://ca.indeed.com/career-advice/career-development/organizational-goals

questions.question: Katrina is interested in investing her money. She is willing to accept some risk for a greater return but doesn’t want to make all the investment decisions on her own. What kind of investment should Katrina consider?
questions.explanation: Mutual funds. A mutual fund is a combination of stocks that can provide great returns in exchange for some risk. Additionally, it usually involves a fund manager who decides on the stocks in the fund, offloading much of the decision making from the investor. This is perfect for Katrina since she can tolerate some risk but doesn’t want to make all the decisions for her portfolio. Trading stocks is generally very risky without professional help and relies on the knowledge and decisions of the investor. Money market accounts are low-risk, low-reward investments. Collectibles are highly risky and would rely fully on Katrina’s decisions.
questions.reference: LAP-FI-077—Invest for Success (Types of Investments)

questions.question: Yamato works at a desk most days and thinks his job is boring and slow. He notices that on days where he has many meetings, collaborates with his coworkers, and talks to different teams or managers, he enjoys his job and feels more productive. What could Yamato conclude about his strengths and weaknesses?

options.A: He works best alone and at a desk.
options.B: He works best with people and activity.
options.C: He is lazy and does not like doing work.
options.D: He has no particular strengths or weaknesses.

questions.explanation: He works best with people and activity. It is important to be able to identify your personal strengths and weaknesses. In Yamato’s case, that fact that he enjoys work and feels better on days where he interacts with many people is an indicator that working collaboratively is one of his strengths. Yamato does not particularly enjoy solitary work, so he does not work best alone. Finding a job boring is an indication that it is not the best fit for Yamato’s strengths, not that he is lazy.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-902—Assess for Success (Assessing Personal Strengths and Weaknesses)

questions.question: Yuna loves animals and values animal rights and protection. She works for a nonprofit organization that rehabilitates and cares for sick pets and strays, which is very fulfilling. This is an example of someone

options.A: adopting values based on their behaviors.
options.B: misaligning their behaviors and their values.
options.C: regularly changing their behaviors and values.
options.D: aligning their behaviors with their values.

questions.explanation: Aligning their behaviors with their values. A person is more likely to be fulfilled if they align their behaviors with their values. In Yuna’s case, working for an animal care center aligns with her value of caring for and protecting animals. Yuna has not misaligned her behaviors and values. There is no indication Yuna’s values changed because of her behavior, and she has not changed her values or behaviors.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-126—Assess Yourself (Assessing Your Personal Behavior and Values)

questions.question: Lars was hired to manage the kitchen of a catering company. Although he is brand new, he wants his employees to respect him and his position. What should Lars do?

options.A: Treat his employees with respect from the beginning
options.B: Let his employees do whatever they want
options.C: Start punishing employees to establish dominance
options.D: Treat his employees poorly until they respect him

questions.explanation: Treat his employees with respect from the beginning. If you want to be respected, you have to respect others. This is especially important when making first impressions with employees. Lars will gain respect if he treats his employees respectfully and fairly. Treating his employees poorly, punishing them, or letting them do whatever they want will cause them to lose respect for him, not gain it.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-021—Make the Honor Role (Acting Responsibly)

questions.question: Shawn is comparing two reports on market growth. Report A is published by a company that sells products in the industry, while Report B is from an independent government bureau. Why is Report B better for objective decision-making?

options.A: It is written by industry insiders who have more real-world experience.
options.B: It is produced by a neutral party with less incentive to bias the data.
options.C: It was primarily created to promote a specific point of view.
options.D: It is likely to have more colorful charts and a modern layout.

questions.explanation: It is produced by a neutral party with less incentive to bias the data. A key part of evaluating sources is identifying bias. Independent or government sources typically lack the conflict of interest that a report from a company within the relevant industry may have. The visual presentation of a report does not determine the underlying objectivity of the data provided. While industry insiders have experience, they can also select data that favor their own products. Material created specifically to promote a point of view is inherently biased and, therefore, less reliable for an objective evaluation of a general market.
questions.piDescription: Evaluate quality and source of information
questions.reference: Purdue University. (2025). Evaluating sources: Introduction. Retrieved January 28, 2026, from https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_inf ormation/index.html

questions.question: Sparkle is a premium laundry detergent company struggling to compete with cheaper generic brands. Instead of lowering prices, the company shifts its marketing to highlight that the detergent allows for high-speed, cold-water washing, saving customers 50% on energy bills. This shift in how the product is perceived is an example of__________ innovation.
questions.explanation: Positioning. Positioning innovation occurs when the purpose of a product is changed. The product itself remains the same, but it is marketed differently. Focusing on the customer’s perception of the products becomes the new goal. Paradigm innovation involves changing the entire institution or industry of the product, such as the shift in personal computers from when they were only in labs to being in every home office. Process innovation would be altering how the product is created, and product innovation involves the actual creation of an original product.
questions.piDescription: Explain the need for innovation skills
questions.reference: LAP-PD-126—Ideas in Action (Innovation Skills)

questions.question: Nicky is reviewing the company’s limited budget for office supplies and the high frequency of printer ink replacements. Which policy should the company implement to manage these resources effectively?

options.A: A procedure requiring employees to print all internal memos in color
options.B: A procedure to remove all printers from the office
options.C: A policy allowing unlimited personal use of office printers
options.D: A policy requiring manager approval for print jobs exceeding 20 pages

questions.explanation: A policy requiring manager approval for print jobs exceeding 20 pages. This policy addresses the company’s limited budget by creating a procedure that decreases the frequency of printer ink replacements, saving the company money. A procedure requiring employees to print all internal memos in color would only increase the frequency of printer ink replacements and cost the company more money. While removing all printers from the office would save the company money, it is unrealistic. Allowing unlimited personal use of office printers would only increase the frequency of printer ink replacements, costing the company more money.
questions.piDescription: Analyze company resources to ascertain policies and procedures
questions.reference: Henry, K. (2025, March 11). Purpose of policies and procedures in the workplace. Retrieved January 27, 2026, from https://www.accountablehq.com/post/purpose-of-policies-and-procedures-in-the-workplace

questions.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of sole proprietorship:
questions.explanation: Unlimited liability. In a sole proprietorship, the business owner is ultimately responsible for the business’s debts and payments. This is known as unlimited liability. Combining capital with another owner is a characteristic of a partnership. Funding through the stock market is a characteristic of corporations. Limited liability is a characteristic of corporations and limited liability companies (LLCs).
questions.reference: LAP-BL-003—Own It Your Way (Types of Business Ownership)

questions.question: In a professional business environment, why is maintaining a clean and appropriate personal appearance considered a form of nonverbal communication?

options.A: It sends a message about your professionalism before you speak.
options.B: It is the only factor an employer uses to determine if you are a good worker.
options.C: It allows you to avoid speaking to customers directly day-to-day.
options.D: It proves that you have more money than the other candidates.

questions.explanation: It sends a message about your professionalism before you speak. Personal appearance is a powerful, nonverbal cue. In business, your image communicates your attention to detail, your understanding of company culture, and your level of respect for the person you are meeting. Appearance complements speech: it doesn’t replace it. You still need strong verbal communication skills to succeed, so it doesn’t allow you to avoid speaking with customers. It is an overgeneralization that personal appearance is the only factor used to determine if you are a good worker. While appearance is important for first impressions, employers also look at skills, experience, and character. Finally, it doesn’t prove you have money to have a clean and appropriate personal appearance. This is because professionalism isn’t about how expensive your clothes are; it’s about being neat, clean, and appropriate for the specific work environment.
questions.reference: LAP-PD-002—Look Good, Feel Good (Personal Appearance)

questions.question: Yolanda manages a team of software developers. She rarely makes decisions without consulting the team first. Yolanda is practicing __________ management.
questions.explanation: Democratic. Yolanda practices a democratic management style by prioritizing input from her employees. Authoritarian or autocratic management would be characterized by tight control over Yolanda’s employees with minimal input. Laissez-faire management would mean Yolanda abdicates most or all decision making to the group.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-037—Can You Relate? (Fostering Positive Working Relationships)
