questions.question: The Leaky Boot, a new themed bar, earns $700,000 in revenue in its first year. $300,000 of this was spent on food, drinks, and other business expenses. $250,000 was spent on employee wages and salaries. An additional $30,000 was spent on promotions and advertising. After deductions, what is the Leaky Boot’s taxable income?
questions.explanation: $120,000. To calculate a business’s taxable income, subtract its deductions from its revenue. Deductions include business expenses such as food and drinks, employee wages and bonuses, and marketing expenses. Adding these values together, we have ($300,000 + $250,000 + $30,000 = $580,000) in tax deductions. Subtracting this from the total revenue, we get ($700,000 - $580,000 = $120,000) in taxable income.
questions.reference: LAP-EC-072—Pay Your Share (Business Taxes)

questions.question: Riss manages a small product development team. How can she best promote a culture of creativity and professionalism?

options.A: By bringing on members who do not share those traits
options.B: By bringing on members who share those traits
options.C: By forcing her employees to act in line with those traits
options.D: By telling her employees how they should behave

questions.explanation: By bringing on members who share those traits. Employees make or break organizational culture, so the employees that Riss brings onto her team will have a massive impact on its culture. Telling or forcing her employees to act in line with her desired culture is unlikely to work in the long run. Bringing on members who do not share Riss’ desired traits would work against her goal.
questions.piDescription: Explain the nature of organizational culture
questions.reference: LAP-EI-064—Culture Club (The Nature of Organizational Culture)

questions.question: Aldin is a music producer. Due to ethical concerns around using AI-generated art, Aldin decides to only use original art made by real people for his album covers. Which of the following is a likely result of Aldin’s decision:
questions.explanation: Greater support from customers. Customers are often more willing and motivated to support businesses they see as ethical. Since Aldin is choosing to avoid AI-generated art, customers who consider AI art unethical are more likely to support him. Using human-made art is likely to increase production costs, decrease risk of legal problems, and increase customer trust.
questions.piDescription: Describe the use of business ethics in entrepreneurship
questions.reference: LAP-EN-044—Ethical Excellence (Ethics in Entrepreneurship)

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a relevant question to ask during a meeting about a new product launch:

options.A: “Who was in charge of product development 10 years ago?”
options.B: “How will the success of this launch be measured?”
options.C: “What time is the company holiday party next month?”
options.D: “What all is included in our company’s insurance plan?”

questions.explanation: “How will the success of this launch be measured?” A relevant question directly relates to the topic at hand and seeks information that helps the team understand goals, expectations, or processes. Knowing who oversaw product development 10 years ago is not relevant to the company’s current launch. Insurance-related questions should be directed to the human resources department, not asked during a meeting about a product launch. Asking about the upcoming holiday party is off topic for a meeting focused on a product launch.
questions.reference: Shah, S. (2022, September 19). How to ask (the right) questions at work. Retrieved January 27, 2026, from https://www.atlassian.com/blog/loom/ask-questions-at-work

questions.question: Marlin starts working as a salesman at a new company. Because he wants to make friends at the company, he spends lots of time with a group of coworkers that he thinks occasionally acts unethically. One possible consequence of this is that

options.A: Marlin will influence them to act more ethically.
options.B: their unethical behavior may hurt Marlin’s reputation.
options.C: Marlin may quickly move up the corporate ladder.
options.D: their unethical behavior will be blamed on Marlin.

questions.explanation: Their unethical behavior may hurt Marlin’s reputation. In the workplace and in life, a person’s reputation is affected by those they associate with. Marlin’s association with a group of unethical coworkers is likely to come back to him and undermine his attempts at making friends and creating goodwill. Spending time with unethical coworkers is not likely to lead to promotions. It is not likely that Marlin will change their behavior. Marlin is not likely to be blamed for the group’s unethical behavior, though he may become associated with it.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-004—Work Right (Demonstrating Ethical Work Habits)

questions.question: Remy lives in an economy with a combination of publicly and privately owned goods and services. Some services like healthcare and education are provided by the government, but many consumer goods like food and clothing are controlled by the private sector. Remy lives in a __________ economy.
questions.explanation: Mixed. Mixed economies take aspects of both socialist and market economies, generally having a mix of public and private ownership of the means of production. A market economy is one in which government’s role in production and distribution is very limited. Traditional economies rely on bartering and trading rather than public and private sectors. Communist economies have a minimal or nonexistent private sector.
questions.piDescription: Explain the types of economic systems
questions.reference: LAP-EC-907—Who’s the Boss? (Economic Systems)

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a business responding to risk by using transference:

options.A: Reducing or controlling a risk's impact
options.B: Choosing not to do something risky
options.D: Moving the impact of risk to someone else

questions.explanation: Moving the impact of risk to someone else. Transference involves moving the impact of a risk to someone or something else and is often used when the impact is measurable in dollars and cents. Common transference devices include insurance, contracts, warranties, and guarantees. Four common risk responses include transference, avoidance, mitigation, and acceptance. A business choosing not to do something risky describes avoidance. A business reducing or controlling a risk's impact describes mitigation. A business accepting a risk's consequences describes acceptance.
questions.piDescription: Explain the nature of risk management
questions.reference: LAP-SM-075—Prepare for the Worst; Expect the Best (Nature of Risk Management)

questions.question: Tanya is writing a proposal to convince a local retailer to carry her new product line. Which approach would be most persuasive?

options.A: Assert that her product is the only good option available.
options.B: Highlight how her product will increase the retailer’s sales.
options.C: List all information relevant to her product in a bulleted list.
options.D: Emphasize the personal financial needs of her business.

questions.explanation: Highlight how the product will increase the retailer’s sales. Effective business persuasion focuses on the benefits to the receiver rather than the needs of the sender. While information about the product is important, that alone does not create a compelling enough reason for the reader to act. “Only option” claims can be perceived as unprofessional and lack the credibility needed for successful persuasion. Business persuasion should be benefit-driven. Focusing on the sender’s personal financial needs is unprofessional.
questions.reference: Indeed. (2025, December 11). 5 persuasive techniques to improve your writing. Retrieved January 27, 2026, from https://www.indeed.com/career-advice/career-development/persuasive-techniques- to-improve-your-writing
reviewNotes: info: rationale does not start with the correct option's text (source wording differs)

questions.question: Lana is an experienced accountant for a large retail company. After being out late the night before, she makes several accounting errors while reviewing an important financial report. The mistakes cause confusion and uncertainty when the report is released. What ethical principle did Lana fail to practice?
questions.explanation: Due care. Due care refers to professional competence and responsibility. Lana was careless enough the night before to impair her performance the next day, leading to important accounting errors that could affect the company as a whole. Lana did not act without integrity, since it was an honest mistake. She did not purposely act against the public interest and did not take biased actions.
questions.piDescription: Discuss the role of ethics in accounting
questions.reference: LAP-FI-351—With Due Care (The Role of Ethics in Accounting)

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the main purpose of import and export laws in international trade:

options.A: To ensure all countries use the same currency
options.B: To regulate the flow of goods across borders
options.C: To eliminate competition for domestic manufacturers
options.D: To grant private corporations the authority to set tax rates

questions.explanation: To regulate the flow of goods across borders. The main purpose of import and export laws in international trade is to regulate the flow of goods across borders through tariffs, quotas, and safety standards. The purpose of import and export laws is not to eliminate domestic competition. Currency regulation is a matter of monetary policy, not import and export laws. The authority to set taxes and trade laws rests solely with governments and international treaties, not private corporations.
questions.piDescription: Explain the nature of import/export law
questions.reference: U.S. Small Business Administration. (n.d.). Know the import and export laws and regulations. Retrieved January 27, 2026, from https://www.sba.gov/business-guide/grow-your-business/export-products/international-sales/know-import-export-laws-regulations

questions.question: Ashwin, chief people officer at Synergize, supports a new employee wellness initiative, promotes it throughout the company, and ensures it remains a priority for the board. Ashwin is a
questions.explanation: Project champion. A project’s champion is its sponsor—perhaps a high-ranking person in the business who has the authority to mobilize the necessary resources to get the project done. The project champion might even be instrumental in selecting the project manager and promoting the project throughout the company. Though the project champion may assist the project manager when obstacles arise, they are not necessarily closely involved in the project. Ashwin is not a project manager, resource manager, or steering committee member.
questions.piDescription: Explain the nature of project management
questions.reference: LAP-OP-158—Projected to Win (Nature of Project Management)

questions.question: Canned goods, vehicles, and household appliances are commonly created using __________ production.
questions.explanation: Mass. Mass production means producing products in large quantities. It is used in the production of such outputs as canned goods, vehicles, and household appliances. Many products that are mass produced have standardized, interchangeable parts. Unit production means producing one item at a time or items in small quantities; it would be used to produce a custom-tailored suit or clean one customer’s carpet. Batch production means producing items in specific amounts, or batches, and is often used to meet specific or short-term market needs. An intermittent production process is one in which production periodically stops and restarts. It can be used in the production of standard products like tools or custom products like individual insurance policies.
questions.reference: LAP-OP-017—Can You Make It? (Nature of Production)

questions.question: Terri needs a financial institution that offers a wide range of services, including commercial loans and investment services. She specifically wants an institution that is for-profit and owned by stockholders. Which type of financial-services provider should she choose?
questions.explanation: Commercial bank. Commercial banks offer a full range of financial services to both individuals and businesses to generate profit for their shareholders. Credit unions are member-owned cooperatives. While they offer similar services, their primary goal is to serve their members rather than stockholders. The primary function of an insurance company is to provide risk management rather than general banking services like checking or business loans. Brokerage firms focus on facilitating the buying and selling of securities rather than providing banking services like commercial checking and lending.
questions.reference: Kagan, J. (2025, July 18). How do commercial banks work, and why do they matter? Retrieved January 28, 2026, from https://www.investopedia.com/terms/c/commercialbank.asp

questions.question: Manuel, a car salesman, senses a customer’s growing anxiety about the monthly payments for a new truck. Manuel advocates to his finance manager to extend the loan term by 12 months. The lower payment puts the customer at ease, and they close the deal. How did having empathy help Manuel?

options.A: It gave Manuel leverage over the customer.
options.B: It made the customer more comfortable.
options.C: It made the customer more vulnerable.
options.D: It gave the customer leverage over Manuel.

questions.explanation: It made the customer more comfortable. Manuel used empathy to identify and solve the customer’s problem, which made them more relaxed and led to a sale. The purpose of empathy is not to gain leverage or take advantage of vulnerabilities, but to understand and address a customer’s issues. Having empathy does not give others leverage over Manuel.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-030—Have a Heart (Showing Empathy for Others)

questions.question: What would be a likely consequence of the U.S. dollar depreciating on the foreign exchange due to low interest rates and high government debt?

options.A: Decreased cost of living in the U.S.

questions.explanation: Increased competitiveness in foreign markets. When a currency becomes weaker, it also becomes more affordable for foreign markets. A weaker U.S. dollar would mean that foreign consumers are more incentivized to buy U.S. goods, making U.S. businesses more competitive in foreign markets. A weaker dollar is likely to decrease consumer confidence, not increase. Similarly, a weaker dollar is likely to increase exports and the cost of living in the U.S., not decrease them.
questions.piDescription: Describe the determinants of exchange rates and their effects on the domestic economy
questions.reference: LAP-EC-100—Get Your Money’s Worth (Exchange Rates)

questions.question: Which of the following actions best demonstrates making a responsible financial decision when managing a business’s cash flow:

options.A: Delaying payments to essential vendors to inflate the current month’s profit report
options.B: Prioritizing the purchase of luxury office decor to impress potential investors
options.C: Utilizing a high-interest credit card to cover long-term expansion costs
options.D: Allocating funds to an emergency fund before committing to capital expenditures

questions.explanation: Allocating funds to an emergency fund before committing to capital expenditures. Responsible financial decision-making involves establishing a reserve to ensure the business can remain operational during unexpected emergencies. Using high-interest debt for long-term projects is financially irresponsible, as the cost of borrowing can quickly outweigh the potential returns of the expansion. Prioritizing the purchase of luxury office decor prioritizes aesthetic appeal over financial stability. Delaying payments to essential vendors is an unethical practice that damages vendor relationships.
questions.reference: Smith, L. (2025, April 11). The basics of financial responsibility. Retrieved January 28, 2026, from https://www.investopedia.com/articles/pf/09/financial-responsibility.asp

questions.question: Juniper, a manager at a small firm, is struggling to manage a rapidly growing workload. Which of the following would be the most effective starting point for her to prioritize her tasks:

options.B: Completing the most difficult tasks first

questions.explanation: Categorizing her tasks by urgency. Prioritizing tasks requires categorizing them by urgency. Evaluating her tasks based on their relative importance and timing allows Juniper to prioritize efficiently. The difficulty of the task does not necessarily correlate with its importance; it would be more efficient to categorize them by urgency before completing any tasks. Rescheduling all upcoming deadlines merely postpones; it does not help Juniper prioritize. Increasing her daily working hours may help Juniper complete her tasks, but it is not an effective starting point for prioritizing tasks.
questions.reference: Dumont, M. (2025, December 31). Top time management strategies for financial professionals. Retrieved March 11, 2026, from https://www.investopedia.com/articles/financial-careers/08/time-management-financial-career.asp

questions.question: Huda’s manager, Silvester, is requesting vendor contract agreements from three years ago to resolve a billing dispute with one of their suppliers. Luckily, Huda refers to a centralized file index to quickly locate the files and share them with Silvester. This is an example of how information management helps
questions.explanation: Save time and money. Managing information appropriately is essential for business success. For a business to run efficiently, information must be managed and organized so it can be found quickly whenever it is needed. And in business, where time is money, this is cost-effective as well. Information management saves businesses time and money by controlling information overload, cutting down on enormous paper trails, and maintaining a higher level of productivity. Because Huda was quickly able to provide Silvester with the contracts, this demonstrates how effective information management helps save time and money. Huda’s ability to locate the files did not necessarily help maintain organizational consistency, comply with laws and regulations, or support decision-making.
questions.piDescription: Discuss the nature of information management
questions.reference: LAP-NF-110—In the Know (Nature of Information Management)

questions.question: Adrienne manages the production floor of a manufacturing plant. Each week, she rotates line workers to a new station or machine. She also gives employees frequent opportunities to learn more about the products they make and how they’re used. One reason Adrienne may do this is to
questions.explanation: Combat job boredom. One disadvantage of job specialization is that it increases boredom on the job, reducing employee morale. Adrienne is combating this by rotating stations and deepening workers’ understanding of the job, giving them variety and a deeper connection with their jobs. These practices are unlikely to reduce waste or increase production speed, as employees learning or adjusting to new stations each week are likely to be more wasteful and less efficient. Similarly, company profit is unlikely to increase as a direct result of Adrienne’s practices.
questions.piDescription: Analyze impact of specialization/division of labor on productivity
questions.reference: LAP-EC-914—Divide and Conquer (Specialization and Division of Labor)

questions.question: To ensure employees don’t accidentally modify important business records, management should save files in a(n) __________ format.
questions.explanation: Read-only. To use today’s information in the future, businesses must have quality records and use an organized system for recordkeeping, whether they are paper or digital. Reliable records are up to date, authentic, trustworthy, and usable. They’re error-free when they’re stored, and they’re error-free when they’re retrieved. By saving digital records in a read-only format, businesses can ensure that their records are tamper-free, as well. Saving important records as editable files opens them up to potential errors. Encryption prevents important business records from being read by unauthorized people, but does not prevent accidental deletion or changes. Compressing business records makes them easier to store, but does not prevent accidental editing.
questions.piDescription: Describe the nature of business records
questions.reference: LAP-NF-001—Record It (Business Records)

questions.question: A coworker asks you, “What did I miss in yesterday's meeting?” What type of question is this?
questions.explanation: Open. Open questions typically begin with "what," "why," or "how." They aren't answered with a simple "yes" or "no." Open questions ask for someone's opinion, knowledge, or feelings. Closed questions are considered "yes or no" questions. It is not likely to be inappropriate for your coworker to ask about yesterday's meeting. Leading questions are usually closed questions that try to "lead" someone to one answer.
questions.reference: Mind Tools. (2025). Questioning techniques: Asking questions effectively. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from http://www.mindtools.com/pages/article/newTMC_88.htm

questions.question: If you are considering the possible consequences of each decision you could make, you are
questions.explanation: Assessing risk. Assessing risk means focusing on the possible consequences and outcomes associated with your decisions and actions. Staying calm, focusing on creativity, and practicing mindfulness are not specifically related to considering the possible consequences of each decision you could make.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-092—Embrace the Unknown (Developing a Tolerance for Ambiguity)

questions.question: A private student loan differs from a federal student loan in that private student loans

options.A: can be made by banks and credit unions.
options.C: are less expensive than federal student loans.
options.D: have terms and conditions set by the law.

questions.explanation: Can be made by banks and credit unions. Private student loans are loans made by private organizations such as banks, credit unions, and state-based or state-affiliated organizations. Private student loans have terms and conditions that are set by the lender. Private student loans are generally more expensive than federal student loans, which are made by the government and have terms and conditions set by the law.
questions.piDescription: Discuss options for financing a college education
questions.reference: Federal Student Aid. (n.d.). When it comes to paying for college, career school, or graduate school, federal student loans can offer several advantages over private student loans. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/loans/federal-vs-private

questions.question: When challenging the status quo, which of the following should you expect to receive from others affected by the change:
questions.explanation: Resistance. When the status quo is challenged, resistance should be expected because people do not like change and usually reject or oppose it. Support and respect cannot be expected from people who will be affected by change.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-134—Unfollow the Crowd (Challenging the Status Quo)

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of ownership investments:
questions.explanation: Collectibles and real estate. Ownership investments are those in which an individual purchases a portion or all of an item. Collectibles (e.g., coins and antiques), real estate (e.g., buildings and land), and stocks (shares of a corporation) are types of ownership investments. With a lending investment, you allow someone to borrow your money for a period of time. In return, you earn a fee or interest on the amount that you lend. Examples of lending investments are savings accounts, money market accounts, certificates of deposit, and bonds.
questions.reference: LAP-FI-077—Invest for Success (Types of Investments)

questions.question: When reconciling bank statements, it is important to consider
questions.explanation: Checks that have not cleared. Reconciling bank statements involves comparing the entries in a checkbook with the entries listed on the bank statement. In many cases, the balance will be different because checks have been written that have not cleared the bank. Therefore, these amounts will not appear on the bank statement. To verify the actual amount in the account, it is necessary to subtract the checks that have not cleared from the balance listed on the bank statement. When reconciling bank statements, it is not necessary to consider the number of transactions, services not available online, or the types of payroll deposits.
questions.reference: Francis, K. (2019, March 11). Steps to manually reconcile a bank statement. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from http://smallbusiness.chron.com/reconcile-bank-statement-1641.html

questions.question: Todd created a graphic organizer to illustrate his business's quality-control processes. He used a combination of pictures, graphs, and simple statements to sequentially present the information. What did Todd develop?
questions.explanation: Storyboard. Business professionals sometimes use graphic organizers to illustrate certain processes or to describe a problem and its solution. A storyboard uses a combination of pictures, graphs, and simple statements to present information in a sequential order. An outline is a general plan giving only the main points of a topic. A draft is the preliminary version of a piece of writing. A proposal is a plan or suggestion. Outlines, drafts, and proposals are not graphic organizers.
questions.piDescription: Apply information to accomplish a task
questions.reference: Miro. (2025). What is a storyboard and how to make one. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://miro.com/storyboard/what-is-a-storyboard/

questions.question: Which of the following is an effective strategy to use before beginning to read:

options.C: Think about what you want to learn.

questions.explanation: Think about what you want to learn. Before beginning to read, it is important to know what you are hoping to learn from reading the text and what you will hope to know after you complete your reading. This will help guide your reading and increase your comprehension. Taking notes is an active reading strategy that you should use while reading, rather than before. Consulting a glossary is a strategy that you can use while reading to increase your understanding of technical or challenging vocabulary. Finally, summarizing is a tactic that can help with comprehension and retention after you have finished reading.
questions.piDescription: Extract relevant information from written materials
questions.reference: Princeton University. (2025). Active reading strategies: Remember and analyze what you read. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://mcgraw.princeton.edu/undergraduates/resources/resource-library/active-reading-strategies

questions.question: It is appropriate for an employee to report their employer's noncompliance with health and safety regulations to the appropriate government agency when

options.A: the employer does not take steps to correct the issue.
options.B: the housekeeping staff disposes of the company's hazardous materials.
options.C: a vendor does not have a ventilation system that meets code.
options.D: a coworker blocks the fire escape route with boxes of old files.

questions.explanation: The employer does not take steps to correct the issue. Businesses must follow certain health and safety regulations to ensure a safe working environment for employees. When employers do not follow regulations, it is important to take action to correct the situation. In many situations, the issue can be resolved easily. For example, an employee might notice that boxes are blocking an exit and tell his/her supervisor about the infraction. Then, the supervisor can take steps to ensure the boxes are moved to an appropriate location. When the employer does not take steps to correct the issue, employees should report the infraction to the appropriate government agency. There is not enough information provided to determine if housekeeping personnel are violating the regulations that govern the way businesses must dispose of hazardous materials. The vendor is not the employee's employer.
questions.piDescription: Report noncompliance with business health and safety regulations
questions.reference: Henderson, K. (n.d.). Employee duties regarding OSHA. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://smallbusiness.chron.com/employee-duties-regarding-osha-1305.html

questions.question: Which of the following can have a negative effect on your health:
questions.explanation: Getting insufficient calories. Humans need to consume enough calories and nutrients to live a healthy life. Eating the right types and amounts of food can help you feel better and stay healthier. Getting insufficient calories can have a negative effect on your health. Standing up straight, using relaxation techniques, and moving your body are all habits that will likely have positive effects on your health.
questions.reference: LAP-PD-002—Look Good, Feel Good (Personal Appearance)

questions.question: Melissa writes checks to pay for her rent, utilities, and groceries, and she keeps a record of all these transactions in her check register. Keeping an accurate check register helps Melissa

options.A: determine when she needs to add funds to her savings account.
options.B: track the amount of money she has spent.
options.C: understand the checking account's restrictions and fees.
options.D: decide when to order new checks.

questions.explanation: Track the amount of money she has spent. A check is a negotiable instrument or bank draft made payable to a specific party for a specific amount of money. A check serves as a written promise to the check bearer that money is available in the issuer's bank account. Checks are a common form of financial exchange. Both individuals and businesses use checks to pay for goods and services such as rent, utilities, food, and supplies. When writing a check, an individual or business keeps a check register that records information about the transaction. This information includes the date the check is written, to whom the check is made payable, the amount of the check, and the check number. The register is a central location to record and track all of the checks written and the amount of money spent. Check registers do not help the check issuers determine when to add funds to a savings account, understand the checking account's restrictions and fees, or decide when to order new checks.
questions.reference: Mycreditunion.gov. (2018, June 29). Understanding a check and balancing a checkbook. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://www.mycreditunion.gov/life-events/checking-credit-cards/checking/balancing-checkbook

questions.question: Which of the following situations best demonstrates why businesses should retain their records:

options.A: A business is planning to send anniversary cards to employees on the date of their employment.
options.B: A business is planning to send press releases to the local newspaper.
options.C: A business is planning to sell out to another company.
options.D: A business is planning to use webinars for employee training.

questions.explanation: A business is planning to sell out to another company. When businesses merge or sell out to other companies, they need to provide records to prove their value to the other companies. Although businesses might retain documentation of employee anniversaries, press releases, and training plans, these records have less significance than records needed to provide proof of a business's income, expenses, and capital investments.
questions.reference: GovOS. (2021, December 17). What is records retention? Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://govos.com/blog/what-is-records-retention

questions.question: An incident report form used by a business would include information about the

options.A: frequency of this type of incident.

questions.explanation: Location of the incident. An incident report form is completed by employees and/or supervisors to report specific details of workplace accidents. Incident frequency and employee history are information that can be obtained by reviewing a file of incident report forms. Medical costs would not be known at the time that the report is completed, but they are important considerations for insurance claims.
questions.reference: Henderson, K. (n.d.). Employee duties regarding OSHA. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://smallbusiness.chron.com/employee-duties-regarding-osha-1305.html

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a noneconomic want:
questions.explanation: Warm, sunny day. A noneconomic want is the desire for something that can be obtained without money. A warm, sunny day does not involve the exchange of money and is considered a free good. A ticket to a rock concert, part-time job, and haircut are examples of economic wants—items that can be valued in monetary terms.
questions.piDescription: Describe the concepts of economics and economic activities
questions.reference: LAP-EC-901—Are You Satisfied? (Economics and Economic Activities)

questions.question: Camille is conducting research for a report about the mercury levels in fish. Which of the following is the most reliable source for Camille to use:

options.A: A newsletter from a nonprofit organization that studies the effects of air pollution
options.B: An online article that was written last month by a well-known marine biologist
options.C: A recent blog entry that was written by Dr. Harold Corning, a retired brain surgeon
options.D: A chapter from a high school physics textbook that was published in 2001

questions.explanation: An online article that was written last month by a well-known marine biologist. An important consideration when evaluating the usefulness, validity, and timeliness of written information is the topic at hand and the author's expertise. A marine biologist studies aquatic life forms, so an article written by this individual is more likely to contain information about fish than a physics textbook, a retired brain surgeon's blog entry, or a newsletter from an organization that studies the effects of air pollution.
questions.piDescription: Evaluate quality and source of information
questions.reference: Harvard University. (2025). Evaluating sources. Retrieved October 7, 2025, from https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/evaluating-sources-0

questions.question: Zack receives a question that he does not understand from a customer. Zack should

options.A: answer the question as best he can.
options.B: transfer the question to a colleague.
options.C: ignore the question and change the subject.
options.D: paraphrase the question and repeat it back to the customer.

questions.explanation: Paraphrase the question and repeat it back to the customer. If Zack does not understand a question, he should restate the question and verify that he understands in order to provide the best legitimate response to the question. Zack should not ignore the question and change the subject because the customer will be dissatisfied. Though Zack should eventually answer the question as best he can, he should first try to clarify. Finally, transferring the question to another colleague might not be possible and should only be used if the misunderstanding cannot be resolved through other means.
questions.reference: Indeed. (2025, June 9) How to respond to questions effectively. Retrieved October 7, 2025, from https://www.indeed.com/career-advice/interviewing/respond-to-questions

questions.question: Should a job applicant let the interviewer know at the end of an initial job interview that they would like to have the job?

options.A: Yes, the applicant should say that they would really like to be hired.
options.B: No, the applicant should wait for the interviewer to offer the job.
options.C: Yes, the applicant can expect to be hired during the interview.
options.D: No, the applicant will seem to be too anxious to find a job.

questions.explanation: Yes, the applicant should say that they would really like to be hired. Job applicants who know that they would like to have the job for which they are being interviewed should let the interviewer know this, usually at the conclusion of the interview. Applicants are seldom hired at an initial job interview, but it helps the interviewer during the selection process to know which applicants seemed most interested in working for the company. The applicant will not seem over anxious, especially if it is phrased in a low-key manner.
questions.reference: Indeed. (2025, June 9). 12 job searching strategies that work. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://www.indeed.com/career-advice/finding-a-job/job-searching-strategies

questions.question: What type of economic resource is being described in the following situations: salespeople waiting on customers, managers instructing employees, and insurance agents selling policies?
questions.explanation: Human. Human resources are people who work to produce goods and services. Natural resources are found in nature and are used to produce goods and services. Capital goods are manufactured or constructed items that are used in the production of goods and services. Resources are considered limited because there are not enough available to satisfy all the people who desire them.
questions.piDescription: Explain the concept of economic resources
questions.reference: LAP-EC-903—Be Resourceful (Economic Resources)

questions.question: Which of the following is an effective way for employees to use the internet to help reinforce their employers' brand and goals:

options.A: Post embarrassing stories about their employers on job listing sites
options.B: Share company news and updates on their personal social media accounts
options.C: Avoid mentioning their employers on their personal social media accounts
options.D: Write bad reviews of their employers on job listing sites

questions.explanation: Share company news and updates on their personal social media accounts. Employees can use the Internet in a number of different ways to reinforce their employers' brand and goals. Some methods for employees to positively impact organizational goals include sharing company news, updates, and job opportunities on their personal media accounts and writing favorable reviews of their employers on job listing sites. Posting bad reviews of and embarrassing stories about employers on job listing sites is likely to hinder organizational goals. If employees don't mention their employers on their personal social media accounts, then they can't help reinforce employers' brand and goals.
questions.piDescription: Describe the impact of a person's social media brand on the achievement of organizational objectives
questions.reference: Lybrand, S. (2023, August 14). What is employer branding and how can it grow your business? Retrieved October 7, 2025, from https://business.linkedin.com/talent-solutions/blog/employer-brand/2018/employer-branding

questions.question: Due to a slump in sales, the RLT Company has decided to lay off 45 workers. Walter, an RLT manager, must choose three employees from within his department to let go. Walter must base his decision regarding the layoffs strictly on facts and data. Walter must be able to defend his decision
questions.explanation: Objectively. Rather than allowing his feelings (positive or negative) for his employees to influence his choice of workers to lay off, Walter must base his decision strictly on facts and accurate data. In other words, Walter must be able to justify and defend his decision, if necessary. Whenever a person uses facts rather than emotions to defend her/his decision or idea, that person is defending his/her decision or idea objectively. Because Walter can defend his ideas objectively, no one can accuse him or his company of playing favorites or choosing to keep a particular worker simply because Walter likes that employee, or because the worker's family has no other income. Subjective ideas are based on emotion, not on fact. There is no indication that Walter will be defending his decision inductively or on a quarterly basis.
questions.reference: Lotich, P. (2020, May 13). 6 tips for managing employee layoffs. Retrieved October 7, 2025, from http://thethrivingsmallbusiness.com/6-tips-in-managing-employee-layoffs/

questions.question: Where can you find information about the work, schedule, and resources for a project?
questions.explanation: A project plan. The compilation of the work, schedule, and assigned resources creates an overall project plan. A code of conduct is a set of rules and standards that govern the expected practices, decisions, procedures, and systems within an organization. A mission statement is a formal summary of the aims and values of a company, organization, or individual. A marketing plan is a set of procedures or strategies for attracting the target customer to a business.
questions.reference: LAP-OP-519—Plan On It! (Planning Projects)

questions.question: What is a major interpersonal reason that people lose their jobs?

options.B: They cannot carry out job tasks.
options.C: They are unable to get along with others.

questions.explanation: They are unable to get along with others. Many people lose their jobs because they are simply not able to get along well with others. You must be able to relate to, and deal effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and customers if you are to keep your job. You can learn how to carry out job tasks, improve self-esteem, and increase technical information, which are not related to interpersonal skills.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-037—Can You Relate? (Fostering Positive Working Relationships)

questions.question: What is one way to develop commitment to your team?

options.A: Split up tasks between group members.
options.B: Collaborate on team guidelines, goals, and expectations.
options.C: Pay attention to teammates' facial expressions.

questions.explanation: Collaborate on team guidelines, goals, and expectations. To reach their goals, team members must be committed to one another and to the team's purpose. One way to ensure that you stay committed is to create a team mission statement or a set of guidelines upon which all members must agree. If you have a say in the expectations and goals, you will be more likely to follow through and remain committed to the team throughout the process. Preparing for any unexpected changes, paying attention to teammates' facial expressions, and splitting up tasks between group members do not necessarily help develop commitment to your team.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-045—Team Up (Participating as a Team Member)

questions.question: An effective technique in conducting a job search is writing to personnel directors and
questions.explanation: Addressing them by name. Addressing personnel directors by their names is an effective technique because the directors often feel that the job seekers are more interested in the positions because they have taken the time to find out the directors' names. Also, letters addressed to a specific person are more likely to be read by that person than letters that are addressed to a general title or office. Usually, it is not appropriate for a job applicant to invite a prospective employer to lunch, ask for an immediate response to an inquiry, or request salary information.
questions.reference: Indeed. (2025, June 9). 12 job searching strategies that work. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://www.indeed.com/career-advice/finding-a-job/job-searching-strategies

questions.question: Patrick is having trouble working with one of his coworkers on a company project. He isn't sure what's wrong, but he knows that his coworker isn't contributing quality work to the project. If Patrick wants to solve this problem, what is the first step he should take?
questions.explanation: Define the problem. When trying to solve a problem, it's important to be sure you know what the problem truly is. For example, Patrick's coworker isn't contributing quality work to their project, but that is actually a symptom of the problem. The true problem could be that Patrick isn't clearly communicating the project's goals, that the coworker is overwhelmed, that the coworker needs more training, etc. Patrick cannot fix his problem until he clearly defines it. Patrick should not ignore the problem or involve another coworker.
questions.reference: LAP-PD-077—No Problem (Demonstrating Problem-Solving Skills)

questions.question: After replacing a light bulb in a ceiling fixture above the selling floor, an employee should immediately
questions.explanation: Put away the ladder. Anything left on the selling floor is dangerous for both customers and store personnel. This includes boxes, hand trucks, or supplies. The other alternatives are activities that might occur after the light bulb is replaced.
questions.reference: Henderson, K. (n.d.). Employee duties regarding OSHA. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://smallbusiness.chron.com/employee-duties-regarding-osha-1305.html

questions.question: Stephanie is leading change at work by organizing a drive to benefit the local food bank. It is the first time her business has undertaken a task like this. Stephanie is using her interpersonal relationships with coworkers to get them excited and involved in the project. Which characteristic of a change leader is Stephanie displaying in this situation?

options.C: Relates to others in a positive way

questions.explanation: Relates to others in a positive way. By using her interpersonal relationships with coworkers to get them involved in change, Stephanie is showing that she can relate to others in a positive way. Change leaders have a sense of urgency, are not afraid to “go for it,” and love to learn new things, but these are not the characteristics Stephanie is displaying in this situation.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-005—Start the Revolution (Leading Change)

questions.question: An employee who comments, "Rules are made to be broken; don't worry about completing those forms correctly," is exhibiting a(n) __________ attitude.
questions.explanation: Negative. Employees who disregard company policies are exhibiting negative attitudes that should be avoided. The other alternatives are desirable attitudes. Individuals who are progressive like to keep up-to-date. Assertive individuals can stand up for their own rights without infringing on the rights of others. Creative people have original thoughts and ideas.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-019—Opt for Optimism (Positive Attitude)

questions.question: Gabriel decides to take a class that will teach him a new skill. He is showing initiative by preparing for
questions.explanation: Advancement. People with initiative, like Gabriel, seek to further their education/training to prepare themselves for personal advancement. For example, it’s often necessary for employees to learn new skills if they want to advance in their companies. Retirement requires a different kind of planning. Most employees do not plan for unemployment or detachment from the business.
questions.piDescription: Explain the importance of demonstrating initiative
questions.reference: LAP-EI-024—Hustle! (Taking Initiative)

questions.question: Rashida has many obligations that fill her schedule every day. She is often running from event to event and rarely has time to complete her work to the best of her ability. Rashida is
questions.explanation: Overcommitted. Being overcommitted means committing to more than what is possible, necessary, or desirable. People who are overcommitted have countless obligations, events, and tasks each day. Their calendars are stuffed to the brim, and they rarely have any free time. A perfectionist is someone who refuses to accept any standard short of perfection. Determining the order of completion based on importance is prioritizing. Goal setting is the ability to visualize, set, and focus on achieving objectives. Rashida is not necessarily demonstrating perfectionism, prioritization, or goal setting.
questions.piDescription: Manage commitments in a timely manner
questions.reference: LAP-EI-077—Commit to It! (Managing Commitments in a Timely Manner)

questions.question: An increase in the amount of income tax people must pay is a change brought about by
questions.explanation: Government. New or revised laws, regulations, policies, public services, leadership, etc., are all types of change brought about by government. They are often the result of economic changes. Changes brought about by individuals are changes concerning their bodies, lifestyles, minds, etc. Changes in society are brought about by shifts in people's values, tastes, habits, etc. Changes brought about by technology are developments, breakthroughs, and discoveries in the fields of science, engineering, etc.
questions.reference: Kagan, J. (2025, August 22). Understanding income tax. Retrieved October 7, 2025, from https://www.investopedia.com/terms/i/incometax.asp

questions.question: While reviewing financial information, Troy noted that the company earned $245,956 in January, $248,122 in February, and $252,878 in March. Which of the following most likely summarizes the company's financial situation:

options.A: Capital assets are depreciating at a slower rate.
options.D: Cash flow continues to be tight.

questions.explanation: Sales are steadily increasing. One reason that businesses analyze financial information is to identify trends. In the example, the company's income has been steadily increasing for three months. Businesses generate income in a number of ways, and product sales are usually the greatest source of income for a business. If sales are increasing, the company may be able to expand or increase the employees' salaries. With the information provided, it cannot be determined if cash flow continues to be tight for the business, if accounts receivable exceeds accounts payable, or if the depreciation rate of capital assets is slower.
questions.piDescription: Describe the need for financial information
questions.reference: LAP-FI-579—By the Numbers (The Need for Financial Information)

questions.question: Determining your personal net worth means finding out how much money you would have if you

options.A: earned twice as much money as you made this year.
options.B: paid all of your debts and purchased more assets.
options.C: sold all of your assets and paid off all your debts.
options.D: sold all of your assets and took on more debts.

questions.explanation: Sold all of your assets and paid off all your debts. Net worth is a single amount representing how much money you would have if you sold all of your assets and paid off all your debts. Net worth does not represent how much money you would have if you paid all of your debts and purchased more assets, earned twice as much money as you made this year, or sold all of your assets and took on more debts.
questions.reference: McGrath, J. (2025). How to determine your net worth. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from http://money.howstuffworks.com/personal-finance/financial-planning/net-worth.htm

questions.question: What is an important consideration when giving employees verbal directions for completing a task?

options.A: It is unnecessary to use demonstrations to support verbal content.
options.B: Employees usually ask questions when they are confused.
options.D: It is best to present information in reverse order.

questions.explanation: Employees process information differently. Because there are different ways that people process information, it is important to consider those differences when providing employees with verbal directions. For example, audio learners are more comfortable with sound and dialogue, so when giving directions, it is beneficial to speak clearly and use terminology that the listeners can relate to. Sometimes this involves using a metaphor or simile to make a point. Diagrams and pictures are often useful when providing directions to visual learners. For learners who are motion-oriented, demonstrating the activity often reinforces the verbal explanation and makes it easier for employees to understand. This might include an actual demonstration or a video of a demonstration. It's always a good idea to ask the employees if they understand the directions because they may be too embarrassed to ask questions—even if they are confused. Presenting the directions in reverse order may confuse the employees.
questions.reference: Harvard University. (2024, January 8). 8 ways you can improve your communication skills. Retrieved October 7, 2025, from https://professional.dce.harvard.edu/blog/8-ways-you-can-improve-your-communication-skills/

questions.question: Failing to manage information properly is most likely to cause a business to

options.D: be shut down by the government.

questions.explanation: Be unprepared for a disaster. Failing to manage information properly is most likely to cause a business to be unprepared for a disaster, whether it's a natural disaster, such as an earthquake, or a technological disaster, such as a system failure. Failing to manage information properly is detrimental to a business, but it doesn't necessarily mean that the business will declare bankruptcy or be shut down by the government. A business may or may not save money on technology costs by neglecting proper information management.
questions.piDescription: Discuss the nature of information management
questions.reference: LAP-NF-110—In the Know (Nature of Information Management)

questions.question: Trayvon wants to change the word “develop” to the word “create” in several places throughout his document. The quickest way to make these changes is by using the __________ function.
questions.explanation: Find and replace. The find and replace function allows computer users to make changes to their documents quickly. This function is beneficial when working with large documents that contain multiple words or phrases that need to be changed. The cut function allows a computer user to remove text or graphics from the document. The paste function allows a computer user to place cut or copied text or graphics in the document. Although the cut and paste functions allow users to change words, they are not as quick as the find and replace function, which is one step. The header and footer function allows a computer user to place document names and page numbers into a document. The styles and formatting function allows a computer user to organize the document's contents in a standard or consistent manner.
questions.reference: Microsoft. (2025). Find and replace text in Word. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://support.office.com/en-us/article/Find-and-replace-text-and-other-data-in-a-Word-document-c6728c16-469e-43cd-afe4-7708c6c779b7

questions.question: How do producers benefit from the exchanges that result from marketing?
questions.explanation: By gaining repeat business. The primary goal of most businesses is to make a profit by gaining and keeping customers. Marketing helps producers to achieve that goal by helping them to effectively plan, price, promote, and distribute their goods and services. Marketing does not always enable producers to increase their charitable contributions or to control costs. All resources are limited.
questions.piDescription: Explain marketing and its importance in a global economy
questions.reference: LAP-MK-901—Have It Your Way! (Nature of Marketing)

questions.question: Because Emma wants to excel in her job, she talks with her manager to get suggestions for ways in which she can improve her efficiency and work quality. Emma is exhibiting an achievement orientation by
questions.explanation: Soliciting feedback. Achievement orientation is a drive to accomplish one's goals and to meet or exceed a high standard of success. Achievement-oriented people often want to do things better or more efficiently than they have been done in the past. To find better ways to do things, achievement-oriented people solicit feedback from others—coworkers, managers, etc. Emma is not setting goals, taking risks, or being patient.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-027—High Hopes (Developing an Achievement Orientation)

questions.question: People are free to make major economic decisions in a __________ economic system.
questions.explanation: Market. A market economy is characterized by limited government control, freedom of choice, private property, freedom of enterprise, profit incentive, and competition. Communist command systems are characterized by government ownership of the means of production and distribution. Socialist command systems combine government and private ownership. Traditional economies produce only what people need, and no major economic decisions are needed.
questions.piDescription: Explain the types of economic systems
questions.reference: LAP-EC-907—Who's the Boss? (Economic Systems)

questions.question: While attending a staff meeting and listening to a coworker present information on the legal use of copyrighted images, Darrell realizes some of the information may not be accurate. What should he do?

options.A: Ask questions to clarify the information
options.B: Don't say anything because it would embarrass his coworker
options.C: Ask for permission to bring the company's attorney to the meeting
options.D: Explain that the information is incorrect

questions.explanation: Ask questions to clarify the information. It is better to ask a question to clarify information than to point out that someone is wrong. Besides, Darrell may not be aware of recent changes in copyright law. Inviting another person to a meeting to prove his point would be considered rude, and others might doubt his ability to trust their judgment or support them in the future. It's important to avoid embarrassing coworkers, but if Darrell has valid concerns, politely sharing them is the best course of action.
questions.reference: Milano, S. (n.d.). Six tips on how to participate in a meeting. Retrieved October 7, 2025, from http://work.chron.com/six-tips-participate-meeting-2014.html

questions.question: Businesspeople often use the calendar app on their mobile devices to
questions.explanation: Track their appointments. Most mobile devices have calendar and scheduling applications that allow users to set and track their tasks and appointments. Mobile devices also include Internet access to check email, text-messaging functions to send text messages to clients, and global positioning systems (GPS), which are navigational tools that help users obtain driving directions.
questions.reference: LinkedIn. (2024, July 30). What do you do if you're an executive needing to stay organized and productive on-the-go? Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://www.linkedin.com/advice/0/what-do-you-youre-executive-needing-stay-organized-as5rc

questions.question: When dealing with disagreeable customers, a helpful guideline is to __________ the customer.
questions.explanation: Listen carefully to. Disagreeable customers are often calmed by employees who remain positive and pleasant, are sincere and respectful, and who listen carefully to what the customer says. It is best to serve these customers as promptly as possible and refrain from pressing them to make a decision. It is not necessary to agree with customers completely and doing so may not make dealing with disagreeable customers easier.
questions.reference: LAP-CR-009—Making Mad Glad (Handling Difficult Customers)

questions.question: A patron asks the server, "Which special do you recommend?" The server has a chance to demonstrate enthusiasm toward
questions.explanation: The product. A high level of enthusiasm for the products they sell is important to marketing employees. It should be part of their goals to exhibit this enthusiasm to patrons in the process of carrying out their duties.
questions.reference: U.S. Department of Labor. (n.d.). Enthusiasm and attitude. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/odep/topics/youth/softskills/enthusiasm.pdf

questions.question: It is important for employees to follow the rules of conduct established by management to

options.A: maintain a consistent and fair work environment.
options.B: reduce the need for professional development.
options.D: ensure that everyone is compensated the same way.

questions.explanation: Maintain a consistent and fair work environment. A firm's rules of conduct outline its policies and expectations regarding employees' behavior in the workplace. The purpose of the rules is to provide consistent behavior among employees, which facilitates a fair work environment. For example, suppose the business expects its employees to be at work by 8:00 a.m., and one employee consistently comes in late. If the late employee is not reprimanded for tardiness, it is not fair to the employees who are following the rules and being responsible. This can create more problems if the responsible employees who arrive on time must pick up the slack for the late employee. Rules of conduct do not ensure that employees are compensated in the same way, nor do the rules of conduct prevent conflict or reduce the need for professional development.
questions.reference: LAP-PD-251—Know the Code (Following Rules of Conduct)

questions.question: While George is unable to work because of a back injury, he receives a check every week for 60% of his usual salary. George's check is a benefit of his __________ insurance.
questions.explanation: Disability. Disability insurance is sometimes called loss-of-income insurance because it pays a percentage of a worker's normal wages to the worker when s/he cannot work because of an illness or injury. It is often purchased through or by an employer. Cash-value is a type of life insurance that pays out the stated value of the policy at the time of death. Liability insurance protects property owners if someone else is injured on or by their property. Bodily injury is a type of liability insurance that protects vehicle owners when they cause injury to others.
questions.reference: Kagan, J. (2025, August 7). What is insurance? Retrieved October 8, 2025, from http://www.investopedia.com/university/insurance/insurance5.asp

questions.question: Orderly and systematic behavior is usually logical and directed toward certain
questions.explanation: Goals. If you are an organized and logical person, you set personal and career goals for yourself. You may be guided by specific rules, encounter barriers, or interact with other people; but your behavior will still be directed toward your goals.
questions.reference: NSLS. (2025). Goal-setting techniques and strategies you can use now for future success. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://www.nsls.org/goal-setting-techniques

questions.question: Which of the following is a true statement about saving and investing:

options.A: A key factor to long-term financial well-being is to start saving and investing early on.
options.B: The need to save and invest is unrelated to the impact of inflation.
options.C: You typically earn more interest on savings accounts than long-term investments.
options.D: Your spending habits have a minimal impact on the amount of money that you save.

questions.explanation: A key factor to long-term financial well-being is to start saving and investing early on. Getting started early is the key to successful investing. The sooner you begin to take advantage of the compounding growth of the stock market, the more money you will have long-term. Inflation is an increase in the cost of goods and services. Over the years, the value of money declines. If you begin to save and invest when you are young, your interest compounds more, making the overall impact of inflation less dramatic. If you have extravagant spending habits, you will not have as much money to save and invest. Investments tend to yield higher returns than interest earned on a savings account.
questions.piDescription: Explain the need to save and invest
questions.reference: Kagan, J. (2025, April 17). What are savings? Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://www.investopedia.com/terms/s/savings.asp

questions.question: Typically, as price increases, supply goes __________ and demand goes __________.
questions.explanation: Up; down. Supply interacts with demand to determine prices. Supply indicates the quantities of an item offered at different possible prices during a specific period of time. Usually, the higher the price of an item, the more of it that will be offered for sale. Likewise, the lower the price of an item, the less of it that will be offered for sale. Demand, on the other hand, reflects the quantities that consumers are willing and able to buy at various possible prices during the same period. Typically, the lower the price of something, the more of it that will be purchased. Also, the higher the price of something, the less of it that will be purchased. Put simply, as price increases, supply goes up and demand goes down. As price decreases, supply goes down and demand goes up.
questions.piDescription: Describe the functions of prices in markets
questions.reference: LAP-EC-906—When More Is Less (Functions of Prices)

questions.question: Rahul and Samantha worked with their attorney to create a will just after they got married. Now, two years later, they have a new baby daughter. Which of the following will need to be added to their will:
questions.explanation: A guardian. A person who has children under 18 years of age should designate a legal guardian to care for them in the event of the death of both parents. Since they already have a will, Rahul and Samantha would already have identified an executor (the person in charge of handling the estate). A power of attorney assigns someone the right to act on a person's behalf. It does not designate a person to care for a child. There is no need to designate a probate court judge in a will.
questions.piDescription: Explain the nature of estate planning
questions.reference: Fidelity. (1998-2025). Estate planning basics. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://www.fidelity.com/life-events/estate-planning/basics

questions.question: Which of the following is affected by consumers' decisions to buy or not to buy:
questions.explanation: Health of economy. The decisions of consumers to buy or not to buy determine the health of the economy. When consumers fail to buy, jobs are lost in retail and wholesale businesses. This forces producers to lay off workers. Consumers who lose their jobs are able to satisfy fewer wants because of decreased income. When consumers buy, the economy grows and prospers. Consumers' buying decisions do not affect the condition of society, the level of government, or the state of democracy.
questions.piDescription: Distinguish between economic goods and services
questions.reference: LAP-EC-902—Get the Goods on Goods and Services (Economic Goods and Services)

questions.question: During taste tests, consumers preferred flavored, naturally sweetened water over the taste of flavored, artificially sweetened water. However, sales data show that consumers predominately purchase flavored water that is artificially sweetened. What can a company correctly conclude from the taste test results and the sales data?

options.A: Consumers purchase artificially sweetened water to avoid excess calories.
options.B: Consumers prefer the taste of flavored, naturally sweetened water.
options.C: Consumers actually prefer the taste of flavored, artificially sweetened water.
options.D: Consumers don't like to drink flavored, sweetened water.

questions.explanation: Consumers prefer the taste of flavored, naturally sweetened water. Based on a taste test, a company can conclude that consumers prefer the taste of flavored, naturally sweetened water. However, sales data cannot accurately conclude consumers' actual taste preferences or buying motivations because sales data do not consider purchasing factors like price, availability, and brand awareness that can affect buying behavior.
questions.piDescription: Draw conclusions based on information analysis
questions.reference: Khan Academy. (2025). Data collection and conclusions. [Video]. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://www.khanacademy.org/test-prep/v2-sat-math/x0fcc98a58ba3bea7:problem-solving- and-data-analysis-easier/x0fcc98a58ba3bea7:evaluating-statistical-claims-easier/v/sat-math-q10-easier

questions.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of solving problems in a group:
questions.explanation: Conformity. When solving problems in groups, there is often a tendency for individuals to want to conform to the consensus. Because of this, people may be less inclined to share ideas that differ from the group. As a result, ideas can be generated and chosen quickly without exploring all other possibilities. Reduced bias, increased risk taking, and greater output are each advantages to solving problems in a group. Bias is often reduced in a group setting because there are many different perspectives. Typically, individual biases can be challenged by other group members and force the individual to acknowledge their biases. Shared responsibility tends to make people more willing to take risks. Output is often greater in a group setting simply due to the number of people involved. The more people you have in a group, the more experience, knowledge, points of view, and ideas.
questions.reference: Its Education Asia. (2005-2024). Solving problems using a group - Advantages and disadvantages. Retrieved October 7, 2025, from http://www.itseducation.asia/article/solving-problems-using-a-group-advantages-and-disadvantages

questions.question: Which of the following would be considered a short-term objective:

options.A: Becoming fluent in a foreign language
options.C: Paying off a twenty-five year mortgage
options.D: Becoming president of a large corporation

questions.explanation: Finishing a six-week computer-software course. An objective is a goal, and a short-term goal is one that takes less than a year to achieve. A six-week course is only a small part of a year. Becoming president of a large corporation, becoming fluent in a foreign language, or paying off a twenty-five year mortgage are long-term goals.
questions.reference: LAP-PD-918—Go For the Goal (Goal Setting)

questions.question: Because Kevin worked late Tuesday evening to complete a report, he was the last employee to leave the building. What procedure does Kevin need to perform to protect the building from unlawful entry?
questions.explanation: Set the security alarm. To reduce the risk of theft, businesses develop procedures for their employees to follow when closing a facility at the end of a work shift. The two most important actions that employees must follow are setting the security alarm and locking the doors. Logging off the computer, locking filing cabinet drawers, and turning off the lights will not protect the building from thieves and burglars.
questions.reference: Baltimore Police Department. (2025). Commercial robbery prevention tips. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from http://www.police.ufl.edu/community-services/robbery-prevention-for-businesses/

questions.question: Troy just accepted a job transfer. As a result, he'll be starting a new job soon in another state. What type of situation requiring adaptability is he facing?
questions.explanation: Unfamiliar conditions. Unfamiliar conditions and situations can be either expected or unforeseen. Troy can certainly plan for his new job and move, but it will still be somewhat unfamiliar to him, and he'll have to adapt to his new circumstances. Troy's situation would not be considered a resource issue, emergency, or personal interaction.
questions.reference: LAP-EI-006—Go With the Flow (Demonstrating Adaptability)

questions.question: Which of the following is a formatting characteristic of a full-block business letter:
questions.explanation: No paragraph indents. Many businesses use the full-block method to format business letters. All components of the letter (date, address, greeting, body, closing, signature block) use left justification, which means all text is aligned on the left margin. Writers using the full-block format do not indent the first sentence of each paragraph. Other formatting characteristics of full-block letters are the use of single-spacing within the paragraphs and the use of double-spacing between the paragraphs.
questions.piDescription: Select and utilize appropriate formats for professional writing
questions.reference: Scribd. (2025). Letter formats: Block, modified block, and semi-block. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://www.scribd.com/document/547025782/Document-1-Docx

questions.question: Aidan is conducting online research for a marketing project at work. What web-based tool will help Aidan save and organize the websites that contain the relevant information he needs for his final report?
questions.explanation: Browser bookmarking applications. Browsers are computer software that retrieve information from the internet. They have bookmarking applications that allow computer users to select websites and store their URLs on a personal computer for easy access in the future. Bookmarking applications allow users to organize sites by categories by placing them into folders on a computer. Notebooks are not online tools. An intranet is an internal network, similar to the internet, that is accessible only by authorized employees. A word-processing memo template formats a type of written message.
questions.reference: Computer Hope. (2025, September 7). Bookmark. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://www.computerhope.com/jargon/b/bookmark.htm

questions.question: A distinguishing characteristic of credit unions is that they

options.C: are unions for people in the banking industry.

questions.explanation: Operate as cooperative financial institutions. Credit unions are nonprofit lending institutions owned by their members. They provide loans to members and may offer a variety of services, but they do not offer more services than banks. The members of a credit union could be individuals who work for the same company, are in the same profession, or belong to the same union.
questions.piDescription: Explain the purposes and importance of credit
questions.reference: LAP-FI-002—Give Credit Where Credit Is Due (Credit and Its Importance)

questions.question: What kind of utility is being created when a producer makes clothing from fabric?
questions.explanation: Form. Form utility is usefulness created by altering or changing the form or shape of a good to make it more useful to the consumer. The producer of clothing creates form utility by making lengths of fabric into clothing that consumers can buy and wear. Time utility is usefulness created when products are made available at the time they are needed or wanted by consumers. Possession utility is usefulness created when ownership of a product is transferred from the seller to the user. Place utility is usefulness created by making sure that goods or services are available at the place where they are needed or wanted by consumers.
questions.piDescription: Determine economic utilities created by business activities
questions.reference: LAP-EC-904—Use It (Economic Utility)

questions.question: Certain health and safety regulations require many types of businesses to
questions.explanation: Routinely inspect equipment. Some businesses operate equipment that may present a safety hazard if the equipment is not operating properly. As a result, certain health and safety regulations require these businesses to routinely inspect equipment to make sure it is safe. In some cases, government inspectors routinely visit the business to inspect equipment. If the inspectors find that the equipment is malfunctioning, they have the authority to force the business to stop using the equipment until it has been repaired and inspected again. Health and safety regulations do not require businesses to purchase new machinery, offer exercise programs, or install security cameras.
questions.piDescription: Describe health and safety regulations in business
questions.reference: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety. (2025, August 28). Prevention and control of hazards. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from http://www.ccohs.ca/oshanswers/prevention/effectiv.html

questions.question: When creating web pages, a business should be sure to include a __________ the home page.
questions.explanation: Link to. A business's website usually contains several pages so specialized information can be explained in more detail. For example, many businesses have pages that describe the history of the company, list the key employees, explain products, offer customer service, etc. It is important that each page include a link to the home page so users can return to the main page easily. Users often want to access each page, and it is easier to do so if they can quickly link to the home page. It is not necessary to include a summary of the home page or a reason for the home page. Businesses often include illustrations or pictures on the home page, although that is not necessary.
questions.piDescription: Create and post basic web page
questions.reference: Masoner, L. (2025, September 10). How to make a website for your small business in 2025. Retrieved Ocotber 7, 2025, from https://www.forbes.com/advisor/business/how-to-make-a-website-for-your-business/

questions.question: A business can protect its confidential computer information from unauthorized users by
questions.explanation: Encrypting computer files. Encryption is the process of transforming information into a secret code so that only specified individuals can read it. By encrypting confidential computer files, the business protects the information from unauthorized access by internal and external sources. For optimal protection from computer viruses, businesses should conduct computer virus scans continuously rather than once a year. Activities such as classifying information and developing internet message boards do not protect the information from unauthorized users.
questions.reference: Gordon, W. (2022, March 11). How to securely store and share sensitive files. Retrieved October 8, 2025, from https://www.popsci.com/store-share-sensitive-files/

questions.question: If you exceeded your project budget, you should

options.A: find a way to increase revenue.
options.B: charge team members for their expenses.
options.C: start the project all over again.
options.D: determine why and whether or not it was worth it.

questions.explanation: Determine why and whether or not it was worth it. Evaluating your finances is one of the most important ways to know whether or not your project could be considered a success. If you exceeded the budget, you should determine why and whether or not it was worth it. You should not start the project all over again because this will only add expenses.
